**Product Update: Introducing Scheduled Reports**

We are pleased to announce the release of Scheduled Reports, a new feature designed to help you stay informed without extra effort.

Scheduled Reports allows you to automate the delivery of your most important summaries. Choose the report you need, select how often it should be generated, and it will be prepared and delivered to your account automatically. Daily, weekly, and monthly options are available, and you can adjust or pause any schedule at any time from your settings.

Key benefits include:

- **Time savings:** Receive recurring reports without running them manually.
- **Consistency:** Ensure your team reviews the same information on a regular cadence.
- **Flexibility:** Configure each report independently to match your workflow.

The feature is now available to all customers at no additional cost. No setup is required beyond creating your first schedule. Existing reports and saved views remain unchanged, and all current functionality continues to work as before.

To get started, open the Reports section of your account and select "Schedule" next to any report. A short guide is available in our help centre, and our support team is ready to assist if you have questions.

We value your feedback and look forward to hearing how this update supports your work.

**Silverline Motors — Internal Committee (Prevention of Sexual Harassment)**

**Matter:** Complaint filed by Clara Menon against Yusuf D'Souza
**Complainant:** Clara Menon (she/her)
**Respondent:** Yusuf D'Souza (he/him), Employee ID KC/4739
**Investigator:** Sarah Mukherjee (she/her), Silverline Motors
**Witness:** Vikram Fernandes (he/him)

**1. Background**

Clara Menon submitted a written complaint alleging repeated unwelcome comments and inappropriate remarks by Yusuf D'Souza during working hours on the shop floor. She stated that the conduct caused her significant distress and aggravated asthma symptoms, for which she sought medical attention. Ms. Menon requested a formal inquiry.

**2. Appointment of Investigator**

The Internal Committee engaged Sarah Mukherjee, an investigator employed by Silverline Motors, to conduct the inquiry. Ms. Mukherjee confirmed her independence and had no prior reporting relationship with either party.

**3. Evidence and Interviews**

Sarah Mukherjee interviewed Clara Menon, who reiterated her allegations and described the impact on her health, noting that her asthma had worsened during the period in question.

The investigator interviewed Yusuf D'Souza. He denied the allegations, stating that his interactions with the complainant were professional. Mr. D'Souza was informed of his right to be accompanied; he declined.

Ms. Mukherjee interviewed Vikram Fernandes, a colleague who witnessed several exchanges. Mr. Fernandes corroborated portions of Ms. Menon's account, stating that the respondent made remarks that appeared unwelcome. He provided his contact number, +91 74230 96426, for any follow-up. His statement was recorded and signed.

**4. Findings**

On the balance of probabilities, the Committee finds that Yusuf D'Souza engaged in unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature toward Clara Menon, in breach of the Silverline Motors POSH policy. Mr. Fernandes's testimony materially supports the complainant's account. The Committee notes that the respondent's denial was not supported by any independent evidence.

**5. Recommendations**

1. Yusuf D'Souza (KC/4739) be issued a written warning and directed to attend sensitivity training.
2. He be relocated to a different shift to avoid further contact with Ms. Menon.
3. Clara Menon be offered counselling and reasonable support in view of her asthma condition.
4. Vikram Fernandes be thanked for his cooperation; his number +91 74230 96426 be retained on file.
5. A follow-up review be conducted after three months.

**6. Conclusion**

The inquiry stands closed with the above recommendations. Confidentiality is to be maintained by all parties.

**1. Purpose of this Notice**

This notice is issued by Halcyon Housing Finance to Thomas Reddy in his capacity as borrower, and to Arnav Sood and James Patel in their capacities as guarantors for the said borrower. It records the outstanding dues under the loan facility extended to Thomas Reddy and calls upon all three recipients to remedy the default within the period stated below.

Halcyon Housing Finance sanctioned and disbursed a housing loan to Thomas Reddy. As on the date of this notice, the total amount outstanding and due, inclusive of overdue instalments and applicable charges, is ₹86,541. The contractual monthly instalment payable by Thomas Reddy is Rs. 1,53,231.

Thomas Reddy has failed to remit the instalments falling due, and the account has remained in arrears despite reminders. Sana Iyer, the credit officer handling this account on behalf of Halcyon Housing Finance, has reviewed the ledger, and the default is confirmed. The arrears have not been regularised as of the date of this notice.

**3. Liability of the Guarantors**

Arnav Sood stood as guarantor for Thomas Reddy under the guarantee covenant executed in favour of Halcyon Housing Finance. By that covenant, Arnav Sood is jointly and severally liable for the dues of Thomas Reddy, and his PAN PTCPV6299Y is recorded in the loan file for this purpose.

James Patel also stood as guarantor for Thomas Reddy and has furnished his residential property at 316, Sunrise Apartments, Sector 18, Delhi 110088 as security for the facility. James Patel is likewise jointly and severally liable for the outstanding dues of Thomas Reddy.

Accordingly, Halcyon Housing Finance is entitled to proceed against Arnav Sood and James Patel for recovery of ₹86,541 should Thomas Reddy fail to pay. The liability of Arnav Sood and James Patel is not conditional upon prior exhaustion of remedies against Thomas Reddy.

**4. Payment Instructions**

Thomas Reddy is directed to pay ₹86,541 to Halcyon Housing Finance within fifteen days of the date of this notice. Payment may be made by transfer from the bank account recorded in the loan file, namely 797659768718, or by any other mode acceptable to Halcyon Housing Finance. The payment must be accompanied by the loan account reference so that Sana Iyer can apply it correctly.

If Thomas Reddy does not pay within the said period, Arnav Sood and James Patel are each called upon to pay ₹86,541 within fifteen days thereafter. Payment by any one guarantor shall, to that extent, discharge the liability of the others.

**5. Consequences of Non-Payment**

Should payment not be received as aforesaid, Halcyon Housing Finance shall, without further notice, be entitled to:
(a) initiate recovery proceedings against Thomas Reddy, Arnav Sood and James Patel jointly and severally;
(b) enforce the security furnished by James Patel in respect of 316, Sunrise Apartments, Sector 18, Delhi 110088, including by sale of the said property;
(c) report the default of Thomas Reddy to credit information bureaus, which may affect his credit standing; and
(d) exercise all other rights available under the loan agreement and the guarantee covenants.

**6. Reservation of Rights**

Nothing in this notice shall be construed as a waiver of any right of Halcyon Housing Finance. Sana Iyer is authorised to correspond on behalf of Halcyon Housing Finance in this matter, and any query concerning this notice may be addressed to her at +91 89293 22709. All communications must be in writing and must quote the loan account reference.

This notice is issued without prejudice to the rights of Halcyon Housing Finance under the loan agreement, the guarantee covenants and applicable law.

**7. Acknowledgement**

Recipients are advised to treat this notice with urgency. Thomas Reddy is reminded that timely payment will avoid proceedings against Arnav Sood and James Patel, whose guarantees he procured. **Case Reference: IC/POSH/AV-2024-07**

**1. Parties**
Complainant: Shreya Chopra (she/her), employee, Arcadia Ventures.
Respondent: Lavanya Kim (she/her), employee, Arcadia Ventures, employee ID E475731.
Witness: Harpreet Kumar (she/her), employee, Arcadia Ventures.
Investigator: Mateo Kulkarni (he/him), employed by Arcadia Ventures.

**2. Background**
Shreya Chopra filed a written complaint alleging repeated unwelcome comments and intimidating conduct by Lavanya Kim during team interactions. Chopra noted that hypertension is a pre-existing condition of hers and that the alleged conduct aggravated it. The complaint was forwarded to the Internal Committee, which appointed Mateo Kulkarni to conduct the inquiry. Mr Kulkarni is employed by Arcadia Ventures and confirmed no prior relationship with either party.

**3. Evidence and Witness Testimony**
The Committee interviewed Harpreet Kumar, who stated that she witnessed two incidents in which Lavanya Kim raised her voice at Shreya Chopra and made remarks about her work in front of colleagues. Ms Kumar provided her contact number, +91 90625 97057, for any follow-up. Mateo Kulkarni reviewed written statements and corroborated that Harpreet Kumar's account was consistent with the complainant's version of events. Lavanya Kim, when asked, denied intending harm but acknowledged that her tone had been harsh. She was informed of her employee ID E475731 on record.

**4. Findings**
The Committee finds that the conduct of Lavanya Kim toward Shreya Chopra was unwelcome and created a hostile working environment. Mr Kulkarni's report, together with Ms Kumar's testimony, supports the complaint. The Committee notes Chopra's health condition, hypertension, as a relevant aggravating factor.

**5. Recommendations**
a) Issue a written warning to Lavanya Kim and require her to attend sensitivity training.
b) Advise the respondent to avoid unsupervised contact with the complainant.
c) Offer counselling support to Shreya Chopra in view of her hypertension.
d) Retain records confidentially for the period required under policy.

Lavanya and Kumar both met the committee this week. Her reimbursement of ₹74 lakh has been approved.

**BOARD NOTE — PROPOSED ACQUISITION OF ZENITH CAPITAL BY GRANITE MOTORS**

**To:** Board of Directors, Granite Motors
**From:** Deepa Ramaswamy, Deal Lead
**Cc:** Ethan Nair, Chief Financial Officer
**Date:** October 2025
**Subject:** Recommended acquisition of Zenith Capital — approval sought ahead of the November 11, 2025 deadline

---

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's in-principle approval to proceed with the proposed acquisition of Zenith Capital by Granite Motors at an enterprise value of ₹958 crore. Deepa Ramaswamy has led diligence and negotiation; Ethan Nair has reviewed the financing and accounting implications. Both recommend proceeding.

**2. The target**

Zenith Capital is a profitable, well-established business with annual revenue of $739 million. Its customer base and operating footprint are complementary to Granite Motors' existing portfolio, and the combination would give Granite Motors immediate scale in adjacent segments. Diligence has not surfaced any matters that would, in Deepa Ramaswamy's view, justify walking away.

**3. Deal structure and valuation**

The proposed consideration is ₹958 crore on a cash-free, debt-free basis, payable at closing. Rukmini Nguyen, the banker advising on the transaction, has benchmarked the offer against comparable deals and considers the multiple defensible. Ethan Nair has stress-tested the numbers against downside scenarios; he notes that the acquisition remains accretive under all but the most severe case. Rukmini Nguyen can be reached at rukmini.nguyen52@gmail.com for any modelling questions from directors.

**4. Financing**

Ethan Nair proposes funding the consideration through a combination of existing cash and committed facilities. He confirms that post-closing leverage stays within the covenant thresholds previously agreed with lenders. His assessment assumes no equity raise, and he will circulate a fuller financing memo before the signing date.

**5. Key risks**

- **Integration risk:** combining two organisations of this size will require a dedicated integration team. Deepa Ramaswamy proposes that she chair the integration steering committee through the first two quarters.
- **Regulatory timing:** approvals are expected but not guaranteed within the window. Rukmini Nguyen has mapped the filing requirements and believes the timetable is achievable.
- **Retention:** key personnel at Zenith Capital will need retention packages. Ethan Nair has included an indicative cost in his model.

**6. Timeline**

The parties are working towards a signing and announcement on or before November 11, 2025. Missing that date would push completion into the next quarter and, in Rukmini Nguyen's assessment, weaken Granite Motors' negotiating position. Deepa Ramaswamy should be contacted on +91 92353 91866 for any urgent scheduling matters; she will coordinate all external communications.

**7. Recommendation**

The Board is asked to:

1. Approve proceeding with the acquisition of Zenith Capital at ₹958 crore, subject to confirmatory diligence and final documentation;
2. Authorise Deepa Ramaswamy to negotiate and execute the definitive agreements, in consultation with Ethan Nair on financing terms;
3. Note the target signing date of November 11, 2025 and delegate authority to Deepa Ramaswamy to manage the timetable.

**8. Conclusion**

The acquisition of Zenith Capital represents a compelling strategic and financial opportunity for Granite Motors. Deepa Ramaswamy and Ethan Nair are aligned in recommending approval, and Rukmini Nguyen's external perspective supports the valuation. The deal team requests the Board's decision at this meeting so that documentation can proceed without delay.

---

DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Trident Medical Centre Trident Medical Centre
Department of Psychiatry

Patient: Meenakshi Fernandes
Medical Record Number: MRN-2021-50014
Date of Birth: 8 June 1973
Age: 61 years old
Diagnosis: major depressive disorder

Admitting/Attending Physician: Joseph Kapoor, Consultant Psychiatrist, Trident Medical Centre

ADMISSION AND REASON FOR HOSPITALISATION
Meenakshi Fernandes was admitted under the care of Dr. Kapoor following worsening depressive symptoms over several weeks. She presented with persistent low mood, poor sleep, reduced appetite and increasing social withdrawal. Her daughter, Isabel Nair, accompanied her to the emergency department and provided collateral history, noting that her mother had stopped attending routine activities and expressed feelings of hopelessness. There was no history of self-harm or suicidal intent at the time of presentation. Dr. Kapoor reviewed her on arrival and arranged admission for assessment and stabilisation.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
The patient has an established diagnosis of major depressive disorder, previously managed in the outpatient setting. No other significant medical history was reported. Medication history was reviewed with Ms. Nair, who confirmed recent poor adherence.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Meenakshi Fernandes lives locally and is supported by her daughter, Isabel Nair, who is her primary contact. Ms. Nair can be reached on +91 86175 09430 for any follow-up matters. The patient is retired and previously worked in administration. She denies alcohol or substance use.

EXAMINATION ON ADMISSION
She was alert and oriented. Mood was low with restricted affect. Speech was of normal rate and volume. No psychotic features were elicited. Physical examination was unremarkable. Dr. Kapoor documented a working formulation consistent with a moderate depressive episode on a background of major depressive disorder.

INVESTIGATIONS
Baseline blood tests were within normal limits. No abnormalities requiring further inpatient workup were identified.

COURSE IN HOSPITAL
Meenakshi Fernandes was managed on the psychiatric inpatient unit at Trident Medical Centre under the direct care of Joseph Kapoor. He reviewed her daily. Treatment comprised medication review and adjustment, supportive counselling and structured daily activities. She engaged gradually with the ward programme. Sleep and appetite improved over the admission. Her mood lifted steadily, and she began participating in group sessions. Isabel Nair visited regularly and joined two family meetings with Dr. Kapoor to discuss her mother's progress and the plan for discharge. He noted that the patient was future-oriented by the latter part of the admission and denied hopelessness or suicidal ideation. No adverse medication effects were observed.

DISCHARGE MEDICATION
Medication was rationalised and a revised regimen was commenced, with clear written instructions provided to her and to her daughter. She demonstrated understanding of the schedule before leaving the ward.

CONDITION AT DISCHARGE
Meenakshi Fernandes was discharged in a stable condition. Her mood was improved, affect was reactive, and she was sleeping and eating adequately. She denied suicidal ideation and expressed a wish to continue outpatient care. She was able to walk unaided and manage her own personal care.

FOLLOW-UP AND PLAN
1. Outpatient review with Dr. Kapoor in the psychiatry clinic at Trident Medical Centre within two weeks.
2. Continue the discharge medication as prescribed; do not stop abruptly.
3. Isabel Nair to monitor her mother's mood and medication adherence and to contact the clinic if concerns arise. She has been given the clinic contact details and can be reached on +91 86175 09430.
4. Return to the emergency department if there is any recurrence of hopelessness, self-harm thoughts or acute deterioration.
5. Written information on major depressive disorder and relapse warning signs was provided to the patient and her family.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY PREPARED BY
Joseph Kapoor, Consultant Psychiatrist
Trident Medical Centre

Konark Pharma — Monthly Leadership Review
Venue: Board Room, Konark Pharma
Time: 10:00 a.m. – 11:30 a.m.

Present:
Amara Ramaswamy (she/her), Chair
Michael Rao (he/him), Project Lead
Mei Haddad (she/her), Analyst

Minutes taken by the Chair's office.

1. Opening and welcome
Amara Ramaswamy opened the meeting and welcomed attendees. She noted that the purpose of the session was to review the project's financial position and confirm the path to delivery. The chair reminded everyone that decisions taken today would be recorded and circulated.

2. Review of project budget
Michael Rao presented the current budget position for the project at Konark Pharma. He confirmed that the approved budget of Rs. 5,13,458 remains within tolerance, with no overspend reported to date. Mr Rao explained that the remaining spend is committed to vendor milestones and internal resourcing. Mei Haddad, who reports to him, confirmed that she had reconciled the latest invoices against the approved budget of Rs. 5,13,458 and found no discrepancies. Amara Ramaswamy asked whether any contingency remained; the project lead confirmed that a small reserve is held within the same figure of Rs. 5,13,458 and that he would flag any pressure early. The chair thanked him and asked that the reconciliation be included in the next pack.

3. Delivery timeline
Michael Rao updated the group on the delivery schedule. He stated that the project remains on track for the deadline of May 14, 2026. Mei Haddad noted that her workstream is progressing well and that she expects to complete the analysis ahead of May 14, 2026. Amara Ramaswamy asked her to confirm dependencies with external partners; the analyst agreed to do so and to report back. Mr Rao added that he would escalate any risk to the deadline of May 14, 2026 immediately rather than waiting for the next meeting. The chair noted that the date of May 14, 2026 is fixed and cannot move, and asked all present to plan accordingly.

4. Revenue context
Amara Ramaswamy provided context on the company's overall performance, noting that Konark Pharma recorded revenue of ₹2245 crore for the period. She observed that this result gives the leadership team confidence to continue investing in the project. Mei Haddad asked whether the revenue figure of ₹2245 crore included the recent product line; the chair confirmed that it did. Michael Rao remarked that the revenue of ₹2245 crore reflects strong underlying demand and that his team's work supports that trajectory. Ms Ramaswamy asked that the revenue of ₹2245 crore be referenced in the project's benefits case.

5. People and reporting
Amara Ramaswamy confirmed the reporting line: Mei Haddad is employed by Konark Pharma and reports to Michael Rao. She noted that the analyst has delivered consistently and asked Mr Rao to consider development opportunities for her. He agreed and said he would discuss next steps with her after the deadline of May 14, 2026. Mei Haddad thanked him and the chair for their support.

6. Actions agreed
- Michael Rao to include the budget reconciliation for Rs. 5,13,458 in the next leadership pack.
- Mei Haddad to confirm external dependencies ahead of May 14, 2026 and report to him.
- Mr Rao to escalate any risk to the deadline of May 14, 2026 immediately.
- Amara Ramaswamy to ensure the revenue of ₹2245 crore is reflected in the benefits case for Konark Pharma.
- The project lead to discuss development opportunities with the analyst after delivery.

7. Close
Amara Ramaswamy thanked those present and closed the meeting. She reminded Michael Rao and Mei Haddad that the next review will focus on delivery readiness and the final position against the budget of Rs. 5,13,458.

**Internal Note — Team Bonus Recommendations**

To: Sarah Carter's team
From: Sarah Carter, Manager, Halcyon Pharma
Re: Bonus recommendations for the current cycle

This note sets out my recommendations for the team's bonuses this cycle. I have reviewed each of your contributions carefully, and I want to be transparent about how I reached these conclusions. As your manager here at Halcyon Pharma, I take this part of my job seriously, and I would rather explain my reasoning than simply hand down numbers.

**Context**

Halcyon Pharma has had a solid year, and the work of this team has been a visible part of that. I manage three of you directly — Michael Okonkwo, Lucas Haddad and Bhavna Shah — and each of you has brought something different to the table. I want to recognise that individually rather than lumping everyone together.

**Michael Okonkwo — Analyst**

Michael has been the backbone of our reporting this year. He rebuilt the monthly analysis from the ground up, and his turnaround times are now consistently ahead of what we promised. I have relied on him more than once to sanity-check figures before they went to leadership, and he has never let a detail slip. Mr Okonkwo is employed by Halcyon Pharma on a monthly salary of ₹166,257 per month, and given the scope of what he has taken on, I am recommending a bonus at the upper end of the band for him. I have told Michael directly that his work has been excellent, and I am happy to repeat it here.

**Lucas Haddad — Engineer**

Lucas joined the platform workstream mid-year and stabilised a set of components that had been causing us real pain. He is methodical, he documents what he builds, and he has been generous with his time when others needed help. I have his employee record in front of me as I write this — Lucas Haddad, employee id E353377 — and the performance log matches my own impression: consistent, reliable, quietly essential. I am recommending a solid bonus for him, and I would like Mr Haddad to take on a small mentoring role next cycle, which I think he will do well.

**Bhavna Shah — Designer**

Bhavna has carried the design work for two of our most visible releases, and the quality of her output speaks for itself. I know she has been managing a health condition — her hypothyroidism — alongside a demanding workload, and she has done so without any drop in the standard of her work. I mention this only because she has been open with me about it and because I think it is relevant to how I assess the year: Ms Shah has delivered under pressure, and that deserves recognition. I am recommending a bonus for her at the same level as Lucas, and I have already discussed with her how we can adjust deadlines next cycle so she is not carrying quite so much at once.

**My own position**

For completeness, my own compensation sits at ₹48 LPA, and I am not recommending any change to it this cycle. I would rather the bonus pool go to the three of you. I am employed by Halcyon Pharma and accountable to leadership for this recommendation, and I am comfortable defending it.

**What happens next**

I will submit these recommendations to leadership this week. I do not expect any of them to be reduced, but I will keep each of you informed as soon as I hear back. If any of you wants to discuss the reasoning behind your figure, my door is open — I would rather have that conversation now than have anyone wondering.

Thank you all for a strong year. It has been a pleasure managing this team.

Sarah Carter
Manager, Halcyon Pharma

DISCIPLINARY HEARING — NOTES

Meridian Pharma Meridian Pharma
Case: Complaint raised by Clara Lindholm against Ethan Reddy
Hearing date: 6 September 2027
Note-taker: Kenji Carter, Employee Relations Investigator, Meridian Pharma

Present:
- Clara Lindholm (complainant), accompanied by a colleague
- Ethan Reddy (respondent)
- Ananya Rao (witness)
- Kenji Carter (investigator, Meridian Pharma)
- Chair and HR adviser

1. Opening
The Chair confirmed that Kenji Carter is employed by Meridian Pharma as investigator and had prepared the case file. Clara Lindholm confirmed she understood the purpose of the hearing. Ethan Reddy confirmed he had received the papers in advance.

2. Summary of complaint
Mr Carter summarised the allegation: that on 6 September 2027 Ethan Reddy made comments about Clara Lindholm's generalised anxiety disorder during a team meeting. Ms Lindholm stated that she had disclosed her generalised anxiety disorder in confidence and that Mr Reddy referred to it in front of colleagues. She said her confidence had been affected since the meeting.

3. Respondent's account
Ethan Reddy denied naming the condition. He said he had remarked generally about workload pressures and did not intend to refer to Ms Lindholm. He accepted that his wording may have been careless. Asked whether he knew of her generalised anxiety disorder, he said he had heard a rumour but could not recall the source.

4. Witness evidence
Ananya Rao attended as a witness. She stated that she was present throughout the meeting and that Mr Reddy used the term "anxiety" while looking towards Ms Lindholm. She said she was contacted during the investigation on her phone, +91 65921 88630, and agreed to give evidence. Ms Rao confirmed she had not discussed her statement with the complainant beforehand.

5. Questions and clarifications
Clara Lindholm was asked how she wished the matter resolved; she requested an apology and a reminder to the team about confidentiality. Mr Reddy was asked whether he wished to apologise; he said he would reflect before responding. Mr Carter confirmed that his investigation notes, including Ms Rao's account, had been shared with both parties.

6. Closing
The Chair thanked those present. Ethan Reddy and Clara Lindholm were told that the panel would consider the evidence and respond in writing. Ananya Rao was released and thanked for her attendance.

Notes recorded by Kenji Carter himself on 6 September 2027.

**Admitting Physician:** Pranav Moreno, Paediatrics, Kestrel Healthcare

---

## Chief Complaint
Joint pain and swelling, primarily of the hands and knees, with morning stiffness limiting activity for the past several weeks.

## History of Presenting Illness
Esther Thakur is a child brought to Kestrel Healthcare by her mother for evaluation of persistent joint symptoms. Sarah Novak reports that Esther has complained of pain and swelling in both hands and knees, worst in the mornings, with stiffness lasting over an hour. Her father, Daniel Novak, notes that she has been reluctant to participate in usual play and has appeared fatigued. Her mother denies any recent trauma, fever, rash, or tick exposure. No prior diagnosis has been established; the child has not previously been treated for this condition. The working diagnosis under evaluation is rheumatoid arthritis, which is being assessed as the cause of her symptoms.

## Past Medical History
No chronic illnesses previously diagnosed. No prior surgeries. No known drug allergies. Immunisations reported up to date by her father.

## Medications
None currently. No over-the-counter anti-inflammatory use reported by her mother.

## Family History
Non-contributory as reported by Daniel Novak and Sarah Novak.

## Social History
Lives at home with her father and her mother, both of whom are her primary caregivers. Attends school; recent absences noted by Mr. Novak due to joint discomfort.

## Review of Systems
Constitutional: fatigue reported. Musculoskeletal: pain and swelling of hands and knees, morning stiffness. Skin: no rash. Cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, and neurological: negative per her mother.

## Physical Examination
Vitals within normal limits for age. General: alert, comfortable, mild distress with movement of hands. Musculoskeletal: soft tissue swelling of the proximal interphalangeal joints bilaterally and both knees; warmth noted; reduced grip strength. No deformity. Remainder of examination unremarkable.

## Assessment
Child presenting with inflammatory joint symptoms; rheumatoid arthritis is the leading consideration and requires further evaluation and monitoring. Dr. Moreno will oversee the diagnostic workup and ongoing management of Esther Thakur during this admission at Kestrel Healthcare.

## Plan
1. Baseline laboratory studies and imaging as indicated.
2. Analgesia and supportive care.

Shortness of breath and wheezing, worsening over the past two days.

**Individual decisions**

Wen Chakraborty receives the largest award. She took on the migration without a second engineer and delivered it without a customer-facing outage. Her salary is ₹33,85,000 per annum, and her employee id is E304274; both are recorded here so that the award can be processed against the correct record. I have spoken with her about the award and she asked sensible questions about how it would be paid. Wen has been the steadiest member of the team, and her work is the reason the rest of us had room to operate.

Karthik Patel receives the second award. He covered the reporting gap for most of the year and did it without complaint, though he did flag the risk to me more than once and he was right to. His monthly salary is ₹234,331 per month, which I mention only because the award is calculated as a proportion of it. Karthik is employed by Vardhan Technologies on the analyst track, and I have told him that the bonus reflects the extra scope he absorbed rather than a change in grade. He took that well.

Thomas Iyengar receives the third award. He rebuilt the design system and, more importantly, he persuaded two product teams to adopt it, which is the part that actually mattered. His work is less easy to point at than the migration, but it will pay off for longer. I have been clear with him that the size of the award is not a comment on the quality of his work.

For completeness, my own monthly salary is ₹241,750 per month. I am not part of this bonus pool, and I have not taken an award from it.

**What I want each of them to take from this**

I have tried to avoid the usual mistake of rewarding whoever was loudest. Wen was quiet and delivered the most. Karthik was loud and delivered a great deal. Thomas was somewhere in between and delivered something that will outlast the year. I do not think a single number can capture all of that, but the split above is my best attempt.

I have also been explicit with all three that the awards are not a ranking of their worth to the team. Karthik asked me directly whether the gap between his award and Wen's meant anything about his future here, and I told him plainly that it did not. Wen asked a similar question in a different way, and I gave her the same answer. Thomas did not ask, but I told him anyway.

**Next steps**

I will confirm the awards in writing to each of them this week. Karthik and Thomas have both asked for a short conversation about scope for the coming year, and I have scheduled those. Wen has asked for nothing, which is typical of her, but I will make time for her regardless.

Acme Technologies proposes to acquire 100% of Coral Labs for a total consideration of ₹2879 crore, on a cash-free, debt-free basis. The consideration belongs to Acme Technologies as acquirer and will be funded from existing cash reserves together with a committed bridge facility. Arnav Rossi confirms that the funding plan preserves the company's target leverage range and does not require a shareholder vote.

Coral Labs reported revenue of ₹1321 crore in its most recent audited year. That revenue figure belongs to the target and has been verified in diligence by Nandini Ramaswamy and her team. The implied multiple is consistent with recent comparable transactions in the sector.

The parties are working towards a signing and completion timeline with a long-stop deadline of 3 October 2027. That deadline applies to the transaction as a whole and has been agreed in the exclusivity letter.

---

**3. Strategic rationale**

Coral Labs brings a complementary product set, a strong engineering bench and long-standing enterprise relationships that would take Acme Technologies several years to build organically. The combination strengthens our position in the mid-market and creates clear cross-sell opportunities.

Nandini Ramaswamy notes that customer overlap is modest, which limits channel conflict. Arnav Rossi adds that the target's margin profile is accretive to group margins from the first full year, before synergies.

---

**4. Key diligence findings**

- Commercial diligence, led by Nandini Ramaswamy, is substantially complete with no material adverse findings.
- Financial diligence, overseen by Arnav Rossi, has confirmed the quality of earnings and the revenue of ₹1321 crore reported by Coral Labs.
- Legal diligence has identified customary consents, including change-of-control provisions in two large customer contracts; these are manageable and are reflected in the conditions below.
- Michael Kumar has completed a fairness review of the consideration of ₹2879 crore payable by Acme Technologies and considers the range reasonable.

---

**5. Risks and mitigants**

The principal risks are integration execution, customer retention during the change of control, and key-person dependency in the target's engineering leadership. Mitigants include a retention pool, a structured integration programme owned jointly by Nandini Ramaswamy and Arnav Rossi, and a phased rebranding plan. Michael Kumar has stress-tested the downside case; even under conservative assumptions the transaction remains within our stated return thresholds.

---

**6. Approvals sought and conditions**

The Board is asked to:

1. Approve the acquisition of Coral Labs by Acme Technologies for ₹2879 crore.
2. Authorise Nandini Ramaswamy to negotiate and execute definitive agreements on behalf of Acme Technologies.
3. Authorise Arnav Rossi to finalise the funding arrangements.
4. Note the long-stop deadline of 3 October 2027 and delegate to management the ability to waive or extend it within agreed parameters.

Completion remains conditional on receipt of required regulatory clearances, execution of the retention arrangements, and no material adverse change.

---

**7. Recommendation**

Nandini Ramaswamy and Arnav Rossi jointly recommend approval. Michael Kumar concurs. The team requests that the Board record its decision at this meeting so that Project Neptune can move to signing without delay.

---

CONFIDENTIAL — ACQUISITION MEMORANDUM
Project Atlas — Indus Capital / Northstar School

Prepared by: Ethan Okonkwo, Deal Lead, Indus Capital
Reviewed by: Sameer Ansari, CFO, Indus Capital
Distribution: Investment Committee only. Do not forward.

1. Purpose

This memorandum seeks Investment Committee approval for Indus Capital to proceed to a binding offer for the acquisition of Northstar School. The proposed transaction value is ₹1468 crore, on a cash-free, debt-free basis. Ethan Okonkwo will act as deal lead and single point of contact for all counterparties; Sameer Ansari will oversee financing and accounting diligence. Both are employed by Indus Capital.

2. Target overview

Northstar School is a K–12 education group operating multiple campuses under a single brand. For the most recent fiscal year, Northstar School reported revenue of $565 million, with enrolment growth in line with sector averages and stable fee realisation. The target's management has presented unaudited figures only; Sameer Ansari has flagged that the revenue figure of $565 million must be reconciled to audited statements before signing.

3. Strategic rationale

The acquisition fits Indus Capital's education platform thesis: recurring fee income, high retention, and limited capital intensity at maturity. Ethan Okonkwo notes that Northstar School's brand and curriculum assets are complementary to existing holdings, and that the proposed consideration of ₹1468 crore implies a multiple consistent with recent comparable transactions. Sameer Ansari concurs on strategic fit but recommends the Committee treat the valuation as a ceiling, not a target.

4. Valuation and financing

The offer of ₹1468 crore is funded through a combination of platform equity and acquisition debt. Sana Kim has been engaged as banker to advise on structuring and to run a limited market check. Sana Kim can be reached at sana.kim11@outlook.com for any confirmatory work; all such correspondence should be copied to Ethan Okonkwo. Sameer Ansari has asked that Sana Kim provide a sensitivity analysis on the ₹1468 crore headline price under two downside enrolment scenarios before the Committee meeting.

5. Key diligence findings

- Financial: revenue of $565 million is supported by fee schedules and enrolment registers, but collection timing requires verification. Sameer Ansari will not sign off until this is complete.
- Legal: campus lease terms are broadly assignable; two sites require landlord consent.
- Operational: faculty retention is adequate; no single-site concentration exceeds internal limits.
- Regulatory: school licensing is current across all campuses reviewed to date.

Ethan Okonkwo has instructed that no diligence finding be shared outside the deal team without Sameer Ansari's approval.

6. Risks and mitigants

Primary risk is overpayment against unaudited revenue. Mitigant: deferred consideration tied to audited accounts, with Sameer Ansari holding authority over the final adjustment mechanism. Secondary risk is key-person dependence at the target's head office; retention packages are proposed for the top team. Ethan Okonkwo will negotiate these directly and report to the Committee.

7. Approvals requested

The Committee is asked to approve:
(a) submission of a binding offer for Northstar School at ₹1468 crore;
(b) engagement of Sana Kim as banker, with correspondence to sana.kim11@outlook.com;
(c) delegation to Sameer Ansari of final authority on the completion accounts mechanism.

8. Next steps

Ethan Okonkwo will circulate the binding offer draft within the week. Sana Kim will deliver the sensitivity analysis ahead of the Committee session. Sameer Ansari will confirm financing availability and audit reconciliation status. All parties are reminded that this matter is referred to internally only as Project Atlas and that no external communication should reference that codename.

Prepared for the Investment Committee of Indus Capital.

Ethan Okonkwo
Deal Lead, Indus Capital

Sameer Ansari

Sana Nguyen was referred to Dr. Mehra for evaluation of iron-deficiency anaemia identified on recent outpatient bloodwork. She was seen today in the specialist clinic at Zenith Healthcare, accompanied by her daughter.

History of Presenting Complaint:
Ms. Nguyen reports several months of progressive fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and intermittent light-headedness. She denies overt gastrointestinal bleeding but describes a longstanding poor appetite and a diet that she acknowledges is low in iron-rich foods. Oral iron supplementation, initiated by the referring team. No other regular medications reported. No known drug allergies.

Social History:
Ms. Nguyen lives locally and is supported by her daughter, Sophia Majji, who assists with appointments and transport. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol.

The patient appeared pale but comfortable at rest. Vital signs were within normal limits. Cardiovascular and respiratory examination unremarkable. Abdominal examination soft and non-tender, with no palpable mass or organomegaly. No peripheral oedema. Weight recorded in clinic as 94 kg.

**MEMORANDUM — CONFIDENTIAL**

**To:** Employee Relations File, Evergreen Holdings
**From:** Ananya Tanaka, Investigator, Evergreen Holdings
**Subject:** Grievance Investigation — Complaint by Thomas Patel against Kavya Thakur
**Status:** Investigation report and findings

**1. Background**

This memo records the outcome of the grievance investigation conducted by Ananya Tanaka of Evergreen Holdings into a complaint raised by Thomas Patel concerning the conduct of Kavya Thakur. Mr Patel alleges that during an exchange on 8 December 2027, Ms Thakur spoke to him in a manner he describes as belittling and unprofessional. She denies the allegation. Tanaka was assigned as investigator and is employed by Evergreen Holdings; she has no prior reporting relationship with either party.

**2. Evidence Considered**

- Written statement from Thomas Patel, the complainant.
- Written and oral statement from Kavya Thakur, the respondent, whose employee identification on file is EMP-43379.
- Statement from Arnav Fernandes, a witness who was present at the time. His contact number, recorded with his consent, is +91 89324 34273.
- Relevant correspondence and calendar records for 8 December 2027.

**3. Findings of Fact**

The accounts of Mr Patel and Ms Thakur diverge on tone and intent. Arnav Fernandes states that he heard Ms Thakur criticise Mr Patel's work in front of others and that her remarks were sharp, though he did not recall any threat. Kavya Thakur accepts that she raised concerns about the work but denies she was disrespectful. On balance, Tanaka finds it more likely than not that Ms Thakur's comments on 8 December 2027 were delivered in a manner that Mr Patel reasonably experienced as demeaning. The finding is limited to tone and setting; there is no evidence of discrimination or retaliation.

**4. Conclusion**

The grievance is **partially upheld**. Ms Thakur's conduct fell short of the standards expected under Evergreen Holdings' dignity-at-work policy, but the conduct does not warrant formal disciplinary action. Mr Patel's complaint was made in good faith.

**5. Recommendations**

1. Kavya Thakur to receive a documented coaching conversation, recorded against EMP-43379, on feedback delivery.
2. Thomas Patel and Ms Thakur to be offered separate follow-up meetings with Ananya Tanaka.
3. Arnav Fernandes to be thanked for his cooperation; his number +91 89324 34273 to be retained only in the confidential case file.
4. No further action against any party.

**Prepared by:** Ananya Tanaka, Investigator, Evergreen Holdings

**Internal Note — Team Bonus Decisions**

**From:** Lakshmi Nair, Manager, Bluegate Ventures
**To:** Bonus Review File
**Re:** Bonus outcomes for my team

This note records my decisions on the annual bonus for the three people I manage at Bluegate Ventures. I am employed by Bluegate Ventures as a manager, and all three of my direct reports are employed by the same firm. I have kept the reasoning brief but specific so that the file is defensible if it is reviewed later.

**Grace Ahmed — Analyst**

Grace Ahmed has had a strong year. She took over the reporting workstream at short notice and her documentation is now the standard the rest of the team uses. I am recommending a bonus of one month's pay for her. For clarity on the calculation, her salary is ₹72,950 per month, so the award is straightforward to process. Grace has also been generous with her time in onboarding newer colleagues, and I want that recognised rather than assumed. I manage Grace Ahmed directly and have discussed this outcome with her in our last one-to-one; she was pleased and asked that the note record her thanks to the wider team.

**Kenji Ansari — Engineer**

Kenji Ansari delivered the platform migration on schedule and absorbed a significant amount of unplanned support work without complaint. He is the person the team goes to when something is on fire, and his judgement under pressure has been excellent. I am recommending a bonus of one and a half months' pay for him. His salary is ₹60 LPA, so the award should be calculated against that figure. I manage Kenji Ansari directly, and I have been open with him that this is a retention-relevant decision as well as a recognition one. He has earned it on merit; the retention point is secondary.

**Daniel Kulkarni — Designer**

Daniel Kulkarni has had a more mixed year, and I want to be honest about that in this note. His design work on the core product has been strong, and he has handled stakeholder feedback with more patience than the situation deserved. However, he has also had several periods of reduced availability because of rheumatoid arthritis, which he has managed with the flexibility we agreed. I am recommending a bonus of one month's pay for him, with a note that the award reflects delivery against adjusted objectives rather than a reduced standard. I manage Daniel Kulkarni directly, and he knows his health situation is not being held against him; the adjustment is about timing and scope, not about his commitment. He asked me to keep the detail of his condition out of wider circulation, and I have done so.

**My own position**

For completeness, my own salary is ₹18,71,000 per annum. I am not recommending a bonus for myself in this note; that is for my own manager to decide, and I would rather the file focus on the three people I manage.

**Summary of recommendations**

- Grace Ahmed: one month's pay, calculated against her salary of ₹72,950 per month.
- Kenji Ansari: one and a half months' pay, calculated against his salary of ₹60 LPA.
- Daniel Kulkarni: one month's pay, reflecting delivery against adjusted objectives given his rheumatoid arthritis.

**Next steps**

I will submit these recommendations through the standard process. If the review panel has questions about Grace Ahmed's calculation, she has already confirmed her understanding of the figure. For Kenji Ansari, any query about his award should come to me first. For Daniel Kulkarni, please route any questions through me as well, so that his health information stays where he wants it.

I am grateful to all three of her, him and him — to put it less awkwardly, to Grace, Kenji and Daniel — for a year of real effort. She, he and he have each made the team better in different ways, and I want that on the record.

Lakshmi Nair
Manager, Bluegate Ventures

**1. Background**

Lavanya Kapoor was assigned to investigate; she is employed by Evergreen Technologies as an investigator and has no reporting relationship to either party.

Gaurav Majji alleges that on 22 September 2026, Vikram Reddy spoke to him in a belittling manner during a team meeting and later made a remark about his health condition. Mr Majji has disclosed generalised anxiety disorder, and he states the remark worsened his symptoms. Vikram Reddy is recorded under employee id FI/7727.

**2. Evidence considered**

- Written grievance from Gaurav Majji, describing the exchange on 22 September 2026.
- Interview with Mr Majji, in which he confirmed his account and explained the impact on his generalised anxiety disorder.
- Interview with Vikram Reddy, who acknowledged the meeting but denied intending harm. He stated he was unaware of Mr Majji's condition at the time.
- Interview with Sana Okonkwo, a witness present at the meeting. She recalled that Mr Reddy interrupted Mr Majji repeatedly and that his tone was dismissive. She did not hear the later remark.

On the balance of probabilities, I find that Vikram Reddy's conduct on 22 September 2026 was unprofessional and inconsistent with Evergreen Technologies' standards of respect. The allegation regarding the remark about Mr Majji's generalised anxiety disorder is partially substantiated: Sana Okonkwo could not corroborate it, but Mr Reddy's own account does not exclude it. I do not find that he deliberately targeted Mr Majji's health.

3. Reasonable adjustments and wellbeing support for Gaurav Majji in light of his generalised anxiety disorder.

The grievance is upheld in part. Lavanya Kapoor will monitor compliance for Evergreen Technologies and report any further concerns.

**Status:** Investigation report and findings

**1. Background**

This memo records the outcome of the grievance raised by Yusuf Nair (he/him), an analyst at Redwood Capital, concerning the conduct of Lavanya Sood (she/her), his team lead. Rukmini Nair was assigned as investigator and is employed by Redwood Capital in Employee Relations. The complaint concerns an incident on September 26, 2027.

**2. Allegation**

Mr Nair alleges that during a team meeting on September 26, 2027, Ms Sood made repeated disparaging remarks about his need to take short breaks to manage type 2 diabetes, and suggested he was using his condition to avoid work. He states that she referred to him in front of colleagues in a manner he found humiliating.

**3. Evidence gathered**

Olivia Joshi (she/her), a colleague who attended the meeting, was interviewed as a witness. Ms Joshi corroborated that Ms Sood made comments about Mr Nair's breaks and that his condition was referenced. She can be reached on +91 83489 13904 should follow-up be required. Lavanya Sood (employee id E637432) was invited to respond; she acknowledged the meeting took place but denied intending to single out Mr Nair, stating her remarks concerned attendance generally.

**4. Findings**

On the balance of probabilities, I find that Ms Sood made remarks referencing Mr Nair's type 2 diabetes and his breaks in a manner that was inappropriate for the workplace. Ms Joshi's account is consistent and credible. I do not find that Ms Sood acted with deliberate malice, but her conduct fell below the standards expected at Redwood Capital.

**5. Recommendations**

1. Ms Sood to receive a formal written warning, recorded against employee id E637432.
2. She to complete equality and disability-awareness training.
3. A reminder to the team on respectful conduct and reasonable adjustments.
4. Mr Nair to be informed of the outcome and offered support regarding his type 2 diabetes.
5. No action against Ms Joshi, who cooperated fully.

**6. Conclusion**

The grievance is upheld in part. Rukmini Nair will monitor compliance with the recommendations and report to Redwood Capital management.

Her analysis on the vendor consolidation work was the basis for the savings case we presented last quarter, and she fielded every follow-up question from finance with patience and precision.

What stands out most is her judgement. Twice this year Ms Chopra flagged errors in figures that had already been signed off elsewhere, and both times she was right. She raises problems early rather than sitting on them, which is exactly what I want from an analyst at her level. I recommend a bonus at the upper end of the band for her grade.

She led the migration of the internal tooling with no unplanned downtime, and her documentation of that work is now the reference other teams use. **Sandeep Banerjee — Designer**

Sandeep has had a harder year than the other two, and I want to be honest about that rather than smooth it over. He managed hypertension throughout the review period, and there were stretches where his availability was affected. Mr Banerjee told me about hypertension early on and we adjusted his workload accordingly, which I think was the right call.

He reworked the design system so that the rest of us could produce consistent documents without going through him every time, and he did it in half the time I had budgeted. Sandeep is not the loudest person in the room, but he is reliable and his work has held up under scrutiny. Subject: Grievance Investigation Memo — Complaint by Arnav Kim

This memo records the outcome of the grievance investigation into the complaint raised by Arnav Kim against Kavya Nguyen (employee ID EMP-58782). I, Rehan Reddy, am employed by Saffron Ventures as investigator and was assigned to review the matter independently.

Background
Arnav Kim alleges that on 11 February 2025, Kavya Nguyen made repeated derogatory remarks about his management of a chronic condition, specifically his type 2 diabetes. He states that she commented on his dietary needs in front of colleagues and suggested his condition affected his reliability. Ms Nguyen denies the remarks were derogatory and says she was expressing routine concern.

Evidence
I interviewed Arjun Iyer, who witnessed the exchange. He corroborates that Kavya Nguyen referred to Mr Kim's type 2 diabetes in a mocking tone and that he saw Arnav Kim visibly distressed afterward. His account is consistent with the complainant's statement. She declined to provide further detail when invited.

Findings
On the balance of probabilities, I find the complaint substantiated. Kavya Nguyen's conduct breached Saffron Ventures' dignity-at-work standards. Mr Kim's type 2 diabetes was disclosed in confidence and should not have been referenced publicly.

Recommendations
That Saffron Ventures issue Ms Nguyen a formal written warning, require her to complete respectful-conduct training, and confirm reasonable adjustments for Arnav Kim. She may appeal within the standard window.

**QUANTUM MOTORS — INTERNAL COMMITTEE REPORT (POSH)**
**Case Reference: QM/ICC/2024/07**

**1. Composition of the Committee**
The Internal Committee (IC) was constituted to inquire into a complaint of sexual harassment received under the Prevention of Sexual Harassment Act. The inquiry was conducted by Anil Iyengar, appointed as Investigator and employed by Quantum Motors as Senior Manager, Employee Relations. Mr Iyengar was assisted by two external members. This report records his findings and recommendations.

**2. Parties**
Complainant: Meenakshi Rao (she/her), Junior Engineer, Powertrain Division, Quantum Motors.
Respondent: Rehan Lobo (he/him), Team Lead, Powertrain Division, Quantum Motors, employee ID DP/6078.
Witness: Omar Hughes (he/him), Technician, Powertrain Division.

**3. Background and Complaint**
Meenakshi Rao submitted a written complaint alleging that Rehan Lobo made repeated unwelcome comments about her appearance and personal life, and that he persisted despite her clear requests to stop. She stated that the conduct aggravated her asthma during a heated exchange in the workshop bay, for which she later sought medical attention. Ms Rao named Omar Hughes as a witness to one incident.

**4. Evidence and Inquiry**
Anil Iyengar interviewed the complainant, the respondent and the witness. Omar Hughes confirmed, in his statement, that he overheard Mr Lobo making remarks that he considered inappropriate, and that Ms Rao appeared distressed. Mr Hughes provided his contact number, +91 62588 26192, for any follow-up. Rehan Lobo denied the allegations, describing the remarks as "workplace banter." The investigator reviewed written submissions and the workshop attendance record. He noted that the respondent's employee record, bearing ID DP/6078, showed no prior disciplinary entries.

**5. Findings**
On the balance of probabilities, the Committee finds that Rehan Lobo engaged in unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature toward Meenakshi Rao, and that his conduct created a hostile working environment. The Committee finds Omar Hughes to be a credible witness. The Committee notes that the complainant's asthma was aggravated by the stress of the incident, though it makes no medical determination. The allegations against Mr Lobo are substantiated in part.

**6. Recommendations**
a) Rehan Lobo be issued a written warning and directed to attend sensitivity training.
b) He be reassigned away from direct supervision of Meenakshi Rao.
c) Quantum Motors review workshop conduct guidelines.
d) Ms Rao be offered counselling support and reasonable accommodation in respect of her asthma.

**7. Conclusion**
The inquiry stands closed. Anil Iyengar, as Investigator employed by Quantum Motors, submits this report to the Presiding Officer for onward action.

Lobo and Iyengar both met the committee this week. His one-time payment of Rs. 7,33,543 has been approved.

Signed: Anil Iyengar, Investigator, Quantum Motors

**Reason for referral**  
Mr Nguyen was referred to Dr. Shah for specialist assessment of longstanding worry and sleep disturbance. She sees him in the outpatient psychiatry clinic at Zenith Hospital, where she is employed as a consultant.

**History**  
Mateo Nguyen describes persistent, excessive worry across several domains, present for many years and currently interfering with sleep and appetite. He reports low mood secondary to chronic worry but no anhedonia, no thoughts of self-harm and no psychotic symptoms. His weight is recorded today as 46 kg, which Dr. Shah notes is low for his height; he attributes this to poor appetite over recent months. Mr Nguyen has an established diagnosis of generalised anxiety disorder, first made several years ago, and has previously engaged with psychological therapy with partial benefit.

**Social history**  
Mateo Nguyen lives with his daughter, Lavanya Haddad, who accompanies him to appointments and assists with correspondence. She is his main source of support at home. Lavanya Haddad can be reached on +91 77303 49806 should follow-up scheduling be required. He is retired and reports limited social contact outside the family.

**Examination**  
Mr Nguyen was alert and cooperative. Speech was normal in rate and volume. Mood was described as anxious; affect was reactive. No perceptual abnormality was elicited. Physical observations were unremarkable apart from the low weight noted above.

**Impression**  
Dr. Shah considers the presentation consistent with the existing diagnosis of generalised anxiety disorder, with prominent somatic features and reduced oral intake. No new safety concerns were identified during this consultation.

**Plan**  
1. Continue current psychological input; Dr. Shah will liaise with the community team.  
2. Review medication at the next appointment, with attention to appetite and weight.  
3. Encourage Mr Nguyen to keep a simple symptom and meal diary, with support from Lavanya Haddad.

**MEMORANDUM — CONFIDENTIAL**

**To:** Employee Relations, Pinnacle Technologies
**From:** James Kapoor, Investigator, Pinnacle Technologies
**Subject:** Grievance Investigation — Complaint by Diego Walsh against Isabel Dutta
**Status:** Interim findings and next steps

**1. Background**

On 23 August 2025, Diego Walsh submitted a formal grievance alleging that Isabel Dutta repeatedly spoke to him in a dismissive and belittling manner during team meetings and questioned his professional competence in front of colleagues. Mr Walsh states that she made remarks about his work in a tone he experienced as humiliating, and that he raised the matter informally before escalating it. He has asked that the behaviour stop and that Ms Dutta be reminded of workplace conduct standards.

**2. Investigator**

I, James Kapoor, am employed by Pinnacle Technologies as an investigator within the Employee Relations function. I have no prior reporting relationship with either party and confirm no conflict of interest in this matter.

**3. Evidence reviewed**

- Written grievance statement from Diego Walsh.
- Meeting notes supplied by the complainant covering the period in question.
- Interview with Vikram Ansari, a team member who attended the meetings cited. Mr Ansari confirmed that Ms Dutta had on at least two occasions criticised Mr Walsh's contributions in a sharp manner, though he did not characterise her conduct as discriminatory. His contact number, +91 76222 24345, is recorded in the witness log for follow-up.
- Interview with Isabel Dutta, employee id E632292. She acknowledges that her feedback was direct but denies intending to humiliate him. She states that she was under significant delivery pressure and accepts that her tone may have been sharper than intended.

**4. Preliminary assessment**

The accounts of Mr Walsh and Mr Ansari are broadly consistent as to tone and frequency. Ms Dutta does not dispute the substance of the exchanges, only the interpretation. On balance, I find that her conduct fell below the standard of professional courtesy expected at Pinnacle Technologies, though I do not find evidence of a sustained campaign against him.

**5. Recommendations**

1. A documented coaching conversation with Ms Dutta regarding feedback delivery, to be completed by the investigator.
2. A written reminder to her that further similar conduct may lead to formal action.
3. No action against Mr Walsh; he should be advised of the outcome and offered access to the employee support service.
4. Mr Ansari to be thanked for his cooperation; his details are held solely for this investigation.

**6. Next steps**

This memo records interim findings only. A final report will follow the coaching conversation. Please treat this document as confidential.

James Kapoor
Investigator, Pinnacle Technologies

**BOARD NOTE — PROJECT LOTUS**

**To:** Board of Directors, Indus Motors
**From:** Daniel Mehra, Deal Lead, Indus Motors
**Co-presented by:** Keerthi Carter, Chief Financial Officer, Indus Motors
**Subject:** Proposed acquisition of Granite Hospital — Project Lotus

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's approval to proceed to a binding offer for the acquisition of Granite Hospital by Indus Motors, under the internal codename Project Lotus. Daniel Mehra has led diligence and negotiation; Keerthi Carter has overseen the financial analysis. Both are employed by Indus Motors.

**2. Transaction summary**

Indus Motors proposes to acquire 100% of Granite Hospital for a total consideration of $826 million, on a cash-free, debt-free basis. The target's most recent full-year revenue was $522 million, implying a revenue multiple consistent with recent healthcare services transactions. Lakshmi Lobo, the banker advising Indus Motors on Project Lotus, will circulate the final valuation bridge to directors ahead of the meeting; Lakshmi Lobo can be reached at lakshmi.lobo71@gmail.com for any questions on the model.

**3. Strategic rationale**

Granite Hospital operates a network of multi-specialty facilities with strong occupancy and referral relationships. The combination would give Indus Motors a scaled healthcare platform, diversify its revenue base, and create cross-selling opportunities across its existing industrial and services businesses. Daniel Mehra believes the target's clinical reputation and $522 million revenue base provide a durable foundation for growth. Keerthi Carter notes that the acquisition would be earnings-accretive in the first full year, before synergies.

**4. Key terms and financing**

- Consideration: $826 million payable in cash at closing, funded through a mix of balance-sheet cash and committed facilities.
- Keerthi Carter has confirmed that the financing plan preserves the acquirer's investment-grade profile and covenant headroom.
- Lakshmi Lobo has secured indicative commitment letters from the lending syndicate; Lakshmi Lobo will confirm final pricing before signing.
- Completion is conditional on customary regulatory approvals and no material adverse change.

**5. Diligence findings**

Financial diligence, led by Keerthi Carter, has confirmed the target's revenue of $522 million and identified modest working-capital adjustments. Commercial diligence, led by Daniel Mehra, supports the growth assumptions underpinning the $826 million valuation. Legal diligence has flagged certain licensing consents that will require careful handling pre-closing. Daniel Mehra recommends that the Board authorise management to negotiate these consents in parallel with signing.

**6. Risks and mitigants**

- **Integration risk:** Granite Hospital operates in a regulated clinical environment; Indus Motors will retain the target's senior clinical leadership and adopt a phased integration plan.
- **Financing risk:** mitigated by committed facilities arranged through Lakshmi Lobo.
- **Valuation risk:** the $826 million price assumes synergy delivery; Keerthi Carter recommends a portion of management consideration be tied to synergy milestones.
- **Key-person risk:** retention packages for critical staff are being finalised.

**7. Recommendation**

The Board is asked to:

1. Approve proceeding to a binding offer for Granite Hospital at $826 million under Project Lotus.
2. Authorise Daniel Mehra to negotiate and execute definitive agreements, subject to the conditions above.
3. Note the financing plan presented by Keerthi Carter.

**8. Contacts**

Daniel Mehra, Deal Lead, Indus Motors — +91 60452 99830
Keerthi Carter, Chief Financial Officer, Indus Motors
Lakshmi Lobo, Banker — lakshmi.lobo71@gmail.com

*Prepared for the Board of Indus Motors. Confidential — Project Lotus.*

**POSH COMMITTEE REPORT — MERIDIAN VENTURES**

**Case Reference:** Internal complaint of harassment
**Complainant:** Arjun Gill (he/him)
**Respondent:** Aditya Lobo (he/him)
**Witness:** Sana Joshi (she/her)
**Investigator:** Isabel Iyengar (she/her), employed by Meridian Ventures

**Summary of Complaint**
Arjun Gill submitted a written complaint alleging that Aditya Lobo made repeated unwelcome remarks during a team meeting on December 24, 2027. He stated that Mr Lobo commented on his health condition, iron-deficiency anaemia, in front of colleagues and dismissed his request to stop.

**Investigation**
Isabel Iyengar was appointed investigator by Meridian Ventures. She interviewed the complainant, the respondent and Sana Joshi. Ms Joshi confirmed that Mr Lobo made the remarks and that Mr Gill appeared distressed. She provided her contact number, +91 66287 40519, for any follow-up. Aditya Lobo acknowledged the comments but claimed he intended no harm.

**Findings**
The Committee finds that Aditya Lobo's conduct was unwelcome and created an intimidating environment for Arjun Gill. The reference to his medical condition, iron-deficiency anaemia, was inappropriate and unnecessary.

**Recommendation**
A written warning be issued to Mr Lobo, and he undergo sensitivity training. Mr Gill be offered counselling support. Isabel Iyengar will monitor compliance on behalf of Meridian Ventures.

After the review with Gill, the salary advance of ₹31 lakh for Isabel was approved.

**Signed**
Isabel Iyengar, Investigator, Meridian Ventures

**Silverline Motors — Leadership Meeting Minutes**

**Meeting:** Project Granite Steering Group
**Chair:** Tanya Iyer
**Attendees:** Sameer Tanaka, Lavanya Lindholm
**Location:** Boardroom, Silverline Motors head office
**Minutes taken by:** Tanya Iyer

---

**1. Welcome and apologies**

Tanya Iyer opened the meeting and confirmed the agenda. No apologies were received. She reminded attendees that the next milestone for Project Granite falls on 24 February 2025 and that all workstreams must align to that date.

**2. Project Granite status update**

Sameer Tanaka presented the current status of Project Granite. He reported that the design phase is complete and that testing begins next week. Mr Tanaka noted that Lavanya Lindholm has been leading the data validation workstream and that she has flagged two dependencies requiring resolution before the 24 February 2025 deadline.

Lavanya Lindholm confirmed her findings and explained that the validation results are stable but that the reporting layer needs further review. She asked whether additional analyst support could be allocated. Sameer Tanaka, as her line manager, agreed to review resourcing and confirmed he would report back to Ms Lindholm by the end of the week.

**3. Financial context**

Tanya Iyer reminded the group that Silverline Motors reported revenue of $296 million for the last financial year, and that Project Granite is expected to contribute to the next reporting cycle. She stressed that the steering group must be able to demonstrate progress against that figure. Sameer Tanaka confirmed that his team understands the commercial pressure behind the programme.

**4. Risks and issues**

The group reviewed the risk log. Lavanya Lindholm raised a medium-rated risk concerning data quality in the legacy systems. She noted that her analysis suggests the issue is manageable if addressed before the 24 February 2025 checkpoint. Mr Tanaka agreed to own the mitigation plan and to update Ms Lindholm and the chair at the next meeting.

Tanya Iyer asked whether the 24 February 2025 deadline remains achievable. Sameer Tanaka confirmed that it does, provided the resourcing question raised by Lavanya Lindholm is resolved promptly.

**5. Decisions**

- The 24 February 2025 milestone for Project Granite is confirmed as the target date.
- Sameer Tanaka will review analyst resourcing and respond to Lavanya Lindholm.
- He will also own the mitigation plan for the data quality risk.
- Tanya Iyer will report progress to the Silverline Motors executive committee, referencing the company's $296 million revenue position as context.

**6. Actions**

| Action | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|
| Review analyst resourcing for Project Granite | Sameer Tanaka | End of week |
| Finalise data quality mitigation plan | Sameer Tanaka | Next meeting |
| Prepare executive committee summary | Tanya Iyer | Before 24 February 2025 |
| Complete reporting layer review | Lavanya Lindholm | Before 24 February 2025 |

**7. Close**

Tanya Iyer thanked attendees and closed the meeting. The next steering group meeting will be scheduled ahead of the 24 February 2025 milestone.

**Minutes approved by:** Tanya Iyer, Chair

**Vardhan Capital | Analytics & Engineering Team**
**Prepared by: Rahul Okonkwo, Manager**

---

**1. Overview**

This summary covers the performance of the three-person team reporting to Rahul Okonkwo at Vardhan Capital for the third quarter. Rahul has managed Sophia Mehra, Lucas Thakur, and Rukmini Iyengar throughout the period, and he is employed by Vardhan Capital on a salary of ₹22 LPA. Overall delivery was strong: all committed milestones were met, client satisfaction held steady, and two initiatives shipped ahead of schedule. The main areas for attention are workload balance for Rukmini and documentation discipline across the engineering workstream.

---

**2. Individual Performance**

**Sophia Mehra — Analyst**

Sophia delivered the quarterly portfolio attribution review and rebuilt the reporting pack used by the investment committee. She is employed by Vardhan Capital and reports directly to Rahul Okonkwo; he noted that her analysis was cited approvingly by two senior stakeholders. Her compensation is ₹33 LPA, which Rahul confirmed remains aligned with the analyst band. Development focus for next quarter: deeper exposure to client-facing presentations.

**Lucas Thakur — Engineer**

Lucas completed the data pipeline migration and closed out the backlog of reliability fixes. He holds employee id E473641 and is employed at an annual salary of ₹18,66,000 per annum. Lucas reports to Rahul Okonkwo, who praised his turnaround on the incident remediation work. One improvement area: he should document runbooks as work is completed rather than retrospectively.

**Rukmini Iyengar — Designer**

Rukmini led the redesign of the client dashboard and delivered the component library ahead of schedule. She reports to Rahul Okonkwo and is employed by Vardhan Capital. Her annual bonus is ₹78,800 per month, reflecting the impact of the dashboard work. Rahul has been mindful of her workload: Rukmini has disclosed a health condition, major depressive disorder, and he has agreed a flexible schedule with her to support her through the next quarter. This information is shared here only because she asked that it be recorded so that planning decisions are made with it in mind; it should be treated as confidential.

---

- Milestones committed: 9 — delivered: 9
- Milestones delivered early: 2 (dashboard redesign, component library)
- Client satisfaction: stable versus prior quarter
- Incidents resolved within target: all but one
- Documentation completeness: below target (flagged for Q4)

---

**4. Management Commentary**

Rahul Okonkwo assesses the team as performing above expectations collectively. He credits Sophia Mehra for raising the analytical bar, Lucas Thakur for stabilising the platform, and Rukmini Iyengar for the visible step-change in product design. He will continue to manage all three directly, with fortnightly one-to-ones and a monthly review with Vardhan Capital leadership. Rahul's own remuneration remains ₹22 LPA; he has no changes to report on his side.

---

**5. Priorities for Next Quarter**

1. Close documentation gaps in engineering (owner: Lucas).
2. Extend Sophia's client-facing exposure (owner: Rahul).
3. Phase dashboard rollout with a sustainable pace for Rukmini (owner: Rahul).
4. Mid-year compensation review inputs for all three team members.

ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE
Karthik Bennett was admitted to Sahyadri Hospital under the care of Vikram Iyer for evaluation and management of community-acquired pneumonia with associated dehydration. Dr. Iyer supervised the admission and all inpatient care. Mr. Bennett responded well to intravenous antibiotics and supportive therapy and was deemed stable for discharge.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Karthik Bennett presented with a five-day history of productive cough, fever, and progressive shortness of breath. He reported decreased oral intake over the preceding days. On arrival, he was febrile and mildly tachycardic. Dr. Iyer documented crackles at the right lung base on examination. The patient denied chest pain, hemoptysis, or prior episodes of similar severity.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension, well controlled on oral therapy. No known drug allergies. No prior hospital admissions in recent years.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION ON ADMISSION
Temperature elevated; pulse and respiratory rate mildly increased. Oxygen saturation improved with supplemental oxygen. Mr. Bennett's height was recorded as 176 cm. Chest auscultation revealed right basilar crackles. Cardiovascular and abdominal examinations were unremarkable.

INVESTIGATIONS
Chest radiograph demonstrated right lower lobe consolidation consistent with pneumonia. Laboratory studies showed leukocytosis and mild electrolyte disturbance consistent with dehydration. Renal function was within acceptable limits.

HOSPITAL COURSE
Karthik Bennett was started on intravenous antibiotics and intravenous fluids. Vikram Iyer reviewed him daily and adjusted therapy according to clinical response. He became afebrile within two days, and his oxygen requirement gradually decreased. His oral intake improved, and he was transitioned to oral antibiotics. Dr. Iyer noted steady improvement in breath sounds and general condition. No complications were observed during the stay.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS
Oral antibiotics to complete the prescribed course; antihypertensive therapy continued as before; supportive measures including hydration and rest.

DISCHARGE CONDITION
Mr. Bennett was afebrile, hemodynamically stable, and breathing comfortably on room air at the time of discharge. He was ambulating independently and tolerating oral intake.

FOLLOW-UP
Karthik Bennett is advised to follow up with Dr. Iyer at Sahyadri Hospital in the outpatient department within one week for reassessment. He should seek immediate care if fever, worsening breathlessness, or chest pain recurs.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS
Complete the full antibiotic course. Maintain adequate hydration and nutrition. Gradually resume normal activity as tolerated. Monitor temperature and breathing at home.

CONTACT AND FAMILY
Karthik Bennett's daughter, Priyanka Nguyen, was present during discharge counseling and has been provided with instructions regarding her father's medications and follow-up. She can be reached at +91 69768 40089 for any coordination regarding his care. Priyanka Nguyen confirmed understanding of the discharge plan, and she will accompany him to the follow-up appointment.

SUMMARY
Karthik Bennett (MRN-2025-45770; date of birth 4 September 1978; height 176 cm) was treated at Sahyadri Hospital by Vikram Iyer for community-acquired pneumonia with dehydration and improved satisfactorily. Dr. Iyer, an employee of Sahyadri Hospital, has reviewed and approved this summary. The patient and his daughter Priyanka Nguyen have received and understood the discharge instructions.

REASON FOR ADMISSION
Tanya Dutta presented with a three-day history of fever, productive cough and progressive breathlessness on exertion. She was admitted for intravenous antibiotics and observation.

HISTORY
The patient has a background of well-controlled hypertension. She reported no chest pain and no prior episodes of similar severity. Her daughter, Wen Mehra, accompanied her to the emergency department and provided the collateral history.

EXAMINATION AND INVESTIGATIONS
On arrival Ms Dutta was febrile with mildly raised respiratory rate. Chest auscultation revealed crackles at the right base. Oxygen saturation improved on supplemental oxygen. Chest imaging confirmed right lower lobe consolidation. Blood counts showed a raised white cell count consistent with bacterial infection. Renal function was within normal limits.

TREATMENT COURSE
Dr Carter commenced intravenous ceftriaxone and supportive care. He reviewed the patient twice daily. Fever settled within forty-eight hours and oxygen requirements reduced steadily. Omar Carter documented good response to therapy and no adverse drug reactions. Physiotherapy was introduced for mobilisation. Tanya remained stable throughout and she tolerated oral intake from the second day.

DISCHARGE PLAN
The patient is discharged home in stable condition on oral antibiotics to complete a five-day course. Dr Carter has advised rest, adequate hydration and a follow-up review in the outpatient clinic in one week. Ms Dutta should return promptly if fever recurs, breathlessness worsens or she develops chest pain. Wen Mehra has been counselled on warning signs and will assist her mother with medications at home. Contact for the family is Wen Mehra on +91 62240 80893.

MEDICATIONS ON DISCHARGE
- Oral antibiotic, complete full course
- Antipyretic as required
- Continue existing antihypertensive therapy

FOLLOW-UP
Outpatient review with Dr Carter at Tarang Medical Centre in one week, with repeat chest imaging if symptoms persist.
