**BOARD NOTE — PROPOSED ACQUISITION OF Arcadia Finserv**

**To:** Board of Directors, Meridian Labs
**From:** Divya D'Souza, Deal Lead, Meridian Labs
**Cc:** Amara Kim, CFO
**Subject:** Project Lotus — Recommendation to Proceed to Definitive Agreement
**Date of note:** Board meeting, current cycle

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's approval to proceed with the proposed acquisition of Arcadia Finserv by Meridian Labs at an enterprise value of ₹1130 crore. Divya D'Souza has led diligence and negotiation; Amara Kim has reviewed the financing and accounting treatment. Arjun Okonkwo of our advisory bank has supported valuation and structuring.

**2. Target overview**

Arcadia Finserv reported revenue of $47 million in its most recent fiscal year, with stable margins and a diversified client base. The target's products complement Meridian Labs' existing platform and would accelerate our entry into adjacent segments. Diligence has not surfaced any material adverse findings; remaining items are customary and manageable.

**3. Deal terms and rationale**

The proposed consideration of ₹1130 crore implies a multiple consistent with recent comparable transactions. The strategic rationale rests on three pillars: revenue synergy through cross-selling, cost efficiency in shared infrastructure, and accelerated product roadmap. Amara Kim has confirmed that the transaction is accretive under the base case and that financing is available within existing covenants. Arjun Okonkwo has provided a fairness perspective on the valuation range; Divya D'Souza will retain Arjun Okonkwo's contact details on file for the signing phase — arjun.okonkwo49@yahoo.com.

**4. Key risks**

- Integration execution risk, mitigated by a dedicated integration office.
- Customer concentration at the target, currently under review.
- Regulatory approvals; counsel advises standard timelines.

**5. Timeline and next steps**

The parties are targeting execution of the definitive agreement by February 18, 2027. Divya D'Souza will coordinate the signing process and can be reached at +91 80345 39256 for any Board queries. Amara Kim will present the financing plan at the next meeting. Arjun Okonkwo will circulate final valuation materials ahead of signing.

**6. Recommendation**

The Board is asked to approve proceeding to definitive agreement on the terms outlined above and to authorise Divya D'Souza and Amara Kim to finalise documentation. Divya D'Souza confirms Meridian Labs' commitment to the timetable; Amara Kim notes that any material deviation in terms should return to the Board.

Submitted for approval,

Divya D'Souza

## Individual Performance

### Ananya Narayanan — Analyst

Ananya Narayanan had a strong quarter. She completed the quarterly forecasting refresh ahead of schedule and her variance analysis was adopted by two other teams. Her stakeholder communication has improved noticeably; Gaurav received unsolicited positive feedback from two department heads about her clear written summaries.

Ananya is employed by Crescent Holdings on a permanent basis. Her current salary is ₹150,460 per month, which Gaurav notes is within band for her grade and level of experience. He recommends her for the advanced modelling training track next quarter.

Deepa's employee ID is EMP-95466, and her salary stands at ₹41,145 per month. Gaurav flags that her compensation should be reviewed at the next cycle given her expanded scope and the market rate for her specialism. She has consistently been the most reliable member of the team on hard technical deadlines.

Development focus: Deepa tends to absorb problems silently; Gaurav has asked her to escalate risks earlier so he can help remove blockers.

### Michael Rossi — Designer

Michael Rossi led the redesign of the internal reporting dashboard, and early user testing shows a marked improvement in task completion time. He collaborated well with Ananya Narayanan on visualising the forecast outputs, and she credited him for making the data far more accessible to non-specialists.

**Internal Note — Team Bonus Review and Context**

**From:** Nandini Patel, Manager, Kestrel Textiles
**To:** Lakshmi Narayanan, Lucas Lobo, Rehan Narayanan
**Subject:** Bonus planning, workload context, and what to expect this cycle

Hello all,

I wanted to put a few things in writing before we sit down individually, so that the bonus conversation is not the first time you are hearing any of this. As your manager at Kestrel Textiles, I owe you clarity rather than surprises, and this note is my attempt at that.

First, the headline. The bonus pool for our team this cycle has been confirmed, and I have submitted my recommendations for each of you. I am not able to share final figures in this note because approvals are still moving through the finance review, but I can tell you that the recommendations reflect the work I have watched each of you do over the past year, not just the last quarter.

For Rehan Narayanan, I want to be direct about something. His annual bonus is set at ₹6,85,000 per annum, and that figure was agreed with finance some time ago as part of his package. I mention it here because Rehan has asked me twice whether the number is still accurate, and I want him to have it confirmed in writing rather than carried around in his head. It is accurate. Separately, and with his permission, I am noting that he has been managing hypertension this year, which has meant a few schedule adjustments and one extended absence. I want to be explicit that this has had no bearing on his bonus recommendation, and I would ask that he not feel himself under any pressure to explain his health to anyone on the team. That is his information to share or not share.

For Lakshmi Narayanan, the picture is a little different because her role has quietly expanded. She came in as an analyst and has effectively been running the demand forecasting workstream since the middle of the year, including the two reviews that went to the leadership group. Her salary is ₹26,17,000 per annum, and I have flagged to finance that this sits below where the market has moved for the scope she is now carrying. I cannot promise an adjustment in this cycle, but I want her to know that I have raised it and that the conversation is open. Lakshmi is employed by Kestrel Textiles on the standard analyst contract, and I have asked HR to review the banding against her current responsibilities.

For Lucas Lobo, the bonus recommendation reflects the platform migration work, which landed on time despite the vendor delays none of us controlled. He has also been the person the newer engineers go to with questions, which is not in his job description and which I have noted in my submission. I have not attached a figure to his recommendation in this note because the approval is still in progress, but I did not want him to read the silence as a signal.

On my own position, for transparency: my salary is ₹249,598 per month, and I am employed by Kestrel Textiles as the manager of this team. I mention it only because I have asked each of you in the past to be open with me about pay concerns, and it seemed fair to say plainly where I sit rather than leave it implied.

A few practical points:

- Individual conversations will be scheduled once approvals are confirmed. I will not discuss one person's figures with another, and I would ask the same of you.
- If you believe the recommendation for you is wrong, tell me directly and I will take it back to finance. I would rather argue the case now than have it sit unresolved.
- Lakshmi, Lucas, and Rehan — you are each managed by me, and any concerns about this note should come to me first rather than to HR or to each other's managers. That is not a rule about loyalty; it is so that I hear the problem while I can still do something about it.

One last thing. Bonus cycles have a way of making people feel ranked, and I want to be honest that some ranking is unavoidable in how the pool is allocated. What is avoidable is people feeling that the process was opaque. If any part of this note is unclear, say so, and I will clarify it in writing so that everyone has the same information.

Thank you for the year's work. I will follow up with meeting times shortly.

Nandini Patel
Manager, Kestrel Textiles

Lumina Labs is a profitable, founder-led business with a strong position in its core market. Its most recent reported revenue was ₹2429 crore, and the business has grown consistently over the past three years. The Board should note that Lumina Labs's revenue figure has been reviewed by Mihir Gill and his finance team and is considered reliable for planning purposes.

**MEMORANDUM — CONFIDENTIAL**

**To:** Kabir Venkatesh, Complainant
**From:** Olivia Ramaswamy, Investigator, Trident Capital
**Cc:** Employee Relations File
**Subject:** Outcome of Grievance Investigation — Allegation Against Keerthi Santos

**1. Background**

This memo records the findings of the grievance investigation conducted by Olivia Ramaswamy, who is employed by Trident Capital as an investigator. Kabir Venkatesh (he/him) filed a grievance alleging that Keerthi Santos (she/her) made repeated dismissive remarks about his medical condition, chronic kidney disease stage 2 (chronic kidney disease stage 2), and excluded him from a team briefing. The conduct is alleged to have occurred on or around 14 September 2025.

**2. Investigation Process**

Olivia Ramaswamy interviewed Kabir Venkatesh on two occasions and Keerthi Santos once. She also interviewed Wen Chopra (she/her), who witnessed the briefing exchange. Wen Chopra's contact number, +91 70543 09572, was recorded in her witness statement for follow-up. Olivia Ramaswamy reviewed the calendar invitation for the briefing and relevant team correspondence. Keerthi Santos was given the opportunity to respond to the allegations and did so in writing.

**3. Findings of Fact**

On the balance of probabilities, Olivia Ramaswamy finds as follows:

(a) During the briefing on 14 September 2025, Keerthi Santos commented that Kabir Venkatesh's "frequent absences were becoming a team problem." Wen Chopra's account corroborates that she made this remark in front of the team.

(b) Keerthi Santos did not invite Kabir Venkatesh to the briefing; Wen Chopra confirmed he learned of it afterwards.

(c) Keerthi Santos was aware of Kabir Venkatesh's diagnosis of chronic kidney disease stage 2 at the time of the remark.

(d) Keerthi Santos's explanation that the comment was a general observation about scheduling is not accepted; the reference to absences, in context, plainly concerned his health-related appointments.

**4. Conclusion**

The grievance is **upheld in part**. Keerthi Santos's remark was inappropriate and inconsistent with Trident Capital's standards of conduct. The exclusion from the briefing is not substantiated as deliberate, as the invitation list was compiled before his return-to-work arrangements were confirmed.

**5. Recommendations**

1. Keerthi Santos to receive a written warning and to complete respectful-workplace training.
2. A reminder to the team on handling health-related absence confidentially.
3. Olivia Ramaswamy to check in with Kabir Venkatesh within four weeks to confirm no recurrence.

**6. Next Steps**

Kabir Venkatesh may request a review of this outcome. Keerthi Santos will be informed separately by Olivia Ramaswamy.

Signed: Olivia Ramaswamy, Investigator, Trident Capital

**Patient:** Ethan Lindholm  
**Date of birth:** November 7, 1990  
**Medical record:** MRN-2021-81047  
**Consulting specialist:** Imran Saxena, Rheumatology  
**Employer:** Coral Healthcare

**Reason for referral**  
Ethan Lindholm was referred to rheumatology for evaluation of persistent joint pain and morning stiffness. Dr. Saxena reviewed his history and confirmed the diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis.

**History**  
Mr. Lindholm reports that symptoms began gradually, with swelling and tenderness affecting the small joints of both hands. He describes morning stiffness lasting longer than an hour, along with fatigue that has interfered with his daily routine. He has no prior history of similar joint disease and no known family history of autoimmune conditions. Ethan denies fever, rash, or recent infection. He states that over-the-counter anti-inflammatory medication has provided only partial relief.

**Examination findings**  
Dr. Saxena observed soft tissue swelling and tenderness in the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints bilaterally. Grip strength was reduced. No joint deformity was noted at this stage. The remainder of the examination was unremarkable.

**Assessment**  
Findings are consistent with active rheumatoid arthritis. Imran Saxena discussed the diagnosis with the patient and explained the expected disease course, the importance of early treatment, and the role of regular monitoring. Mr. Lindholm was advised on joint protection and appropriate exercise.

**Plan**  
Dr. Saxena will initiate disease-modifying therapy and arrange baseline bloodwork before the next visit. Ethan should continue symptomatic relief as discussed and report any new or worsening symptoms promptly. **Case Reference:** QV/POSH/2025/03
**Complainant:** Kenji Gill (he/him)
**Respondent:** Yusuf Majji (he/him), employee id YE/0994
**Investigator:** Aditya Ahmed (he/him), employed by Quantum Ventures
**Witness:** Sven Reddy (he/him)
**Date of alleged incident:** 24 March 2025

**1. Background**

Kenji Gill submitted a written complaint alleging inappropriate and unwelcome conduct by Yusuf Majji during a team interaction on 24 March 2025. Kenji reported that the conduct aggravated a pre-existing health condition, namely his migraine, and that Mr Majji continued the behaviour after being asked to stop. Aditya Ahmed was appointed as investigator by Quantum Ventures to examine the allegations.

**2. Evidence and Interviews**

Aditya Ahmed interviewed Kenji Gill, Yusuf Majji and Sven Reddy. Sven Reddy, who was present throughout, corroborated Kenji's account, stating that Mr Majji made repeated remarks after the complainant requested that he stop. Mr Reddy further noted that Kenji appeared unwell and mentioned his migraine during the exchange.

In his interview, Yusuf Majji acknowledged being present but denied that his remarks were unwelcome. Aditya Ahmed reviewed the attendance record confirming the respondent's employee id YE/0994 and the timing of the interaction on 24 March 2025. Mr Ahmed found Sven Reddy's testimony consistent and credible.

**3. Findings**

The Committee, having reviewed Aditya Ahmed's investigation report, finds that:

- The conduct of Yusuf Majji on 24 March 2025 was unwelcome and persisted after a clear request to stop;
- His behaviour contributed to the deterioration of Kenji Gill's migraine during the interaction;
- Sven Reddy's independent account supports the complainant's version of events.

The Committee notes that Aditya Ahmed, as an employee of Quantum Ventures, conducted the inquiry in accordance with the organisation's policy.

**4. Recommendations**

1. A written warning be issued to Yusuf Majji (employee id YE/0994) regarding his conduct.
2. Mr Majji undergo mandatory sensitivity training.
3. Quantum Ventures review its reporting channels to ensure timely escalation.
4. Kenji Gill be offered appropriate support, including consideration of his migraine-related needs.

**5. Conclusion**

The complaint is upheld. Aditya Ahmed's findings are accepted by the Committee. Kenji Gill and Yusuf Majji shall each receive a copy of this report.

Submitted by the Internal Committee, Quantum Ventures.

# ADMISSION NOTE

**Patient:** Amara Moreno

**Sex:** Female

## Source of History

History obtained from Ananya Moreno, mother of Amara Moreno, and Ethan Moreno, father. Both parents are present and provide consistent accounts. The child is alert and contributes to her own history where able.

## Chief Complaint

Fatigue and pallor, worsening over several weeks.

## History of Presenting Illness

Amara Moreno is a 10 years old girl brought to Redwood Medical Centre by her mother and her father with progressive tiredness, reduced play tolerance, and noticeable pallor noted by Ananya Moreno at home. Ethan Moreno reports that she has been sleeping more than usual and has had difficulty concentrating at school. No fever, no bleeding, no recent infections. Appetite has been poor. The patient has a known background of iron-deficiency anaemia, for which she has been under follow-up. Her mother confirms intermittent adherence to oral iron, and the father notes that she often refuses the tablets.

On direct questioning, Amara describes feeling "dizzy when I stand up" but denies chest pain, palpitations, or breathlessness at rest. No pica, no melena, no haematuria.

## Past Medical History

- Iron-deficiency anaemia — diagnosed previously, on oral iron supplementation.
- No other chronic illness reported by Ananya Moreno or Ethan Moreno.
- No previous surgeries. No known allergies.

## Medications

Oral iron supplement, dose and frequency as previously prescribed. The mother reports irregular administration over the past month.

## Immunisations

Reported up to date by Ethan Moreno; records to be requested from the family's usual provider.

## Family History

No family history of haematological disorder. Ananya Moreno and Ethan Moreno are both well. No consanguinity.

## Social History

Amara lives with her mother and her father. She attends school. No safeguarding concerns identified during interview with Ananya Moreno and Ethan Moreno.

## Examination

- General: alert, pale, no distress.
- Vital signs: within normal limits for age; no postural drop documented on this assessment.
- Cardiovascular: soft systolic murmur, no gallop.
- Respiratory: clear bilaterally.
- Abdomen: soft, non-tender, no organomegaly.
- Neurological: grossly intact.

## Impression

Amara Moreno presents with symptomatic iron-deficiency anaemia requiring inpatient assessment and management. Kenji Kapoor has reviewed the patient and agrees with admission.

## Plan

1. Admit to paediatric ward under Dr. Kapoor, who will supervise her care.
2. Baseline bloods including full blood count, iron studies, and reticulocyte count.

4. Monitor for symptomatic improvement; reassess need for further investigation if response is poor.

- Hospital deposit for Amara Moreno: ₹7,98,000 — received and receipted.
- Contact numbers held on file: Ethan Moreno — +91 97908 39354; Ananya Moreno — +91 86500 01045.
- Identification: Ananya Moreno's Aadhaar 4136 4325 5268 verified for registration purposes.

## Consent

Admission consent discussed with Ananya Moreno and Ethan Moreno as parents of Amara Moreno. Both mother and father consented. The child assented.

- Hiroshi Banerjee, complainant (he/him)
- Esther Nair, respondent (she/her), employee id EMP-29260
- Ethan Novak, witness (he/him)

**1. Opening**
Nandini Santos opened the hearing and confirmed that Halcyon Ventures had commissioned her investigation into the grievance. She reminded all parties of confidentiality and explained that the panel would consider the events of 5 January 2024.

**2. Complainant's account**
Hiroshi Banerjee stated that on 5 January 2024 Esther Nair made repeated comments about his health condition, hypothyroidism, which he found humiliating. Mr Banerjee said he had asked her to stop. He confirmed that his medical information had been shared with the team without his consent.

**3. Respondent's account**
Esther Nair denied mocking Mr Banerjee. She accepted that she had mentioned his condition in a team meeting but said she believed it was common knowledge. Ms Nair apologised for any upset caused. She confirmed her employee id, EMP-29260, for the record.

**4. Witness evidence**
Ethan Novak stated that he was present on 5 January 2024 and heard the exchange. He recalled that Ms Nair referred to Mr Banerjee's condition in a joking manner. He said Mr Banerjee appeared distressed afterwards. Ethan Novak confirmed that a contact number, +91 81280 36828, had been used to arrange a follow-up call about the incident; he could not recall whether the number belonged to him or to him.

**5. Questions from the panel**
Nandini Santos asked Ms Nair whether she understood why the comments were inappropriate. She said she did now. Dr Santos asked Mr Novak whether he had reported the matter at the time; he said he had not. The investigator noted that Mr Banerjee's condition, hypothyroidism, is a protected health matter.

**6. Closing**
Nandini Santos thanked those present. She confirmed that Halcyon Ventures would issue its findings in writing. Ms Nair and Mr Novak were reminded of their and his respective obligations. The hearing closed.

SPECIALIST CONSULTATION NOTE

Coral Healthcare — Department of Rheumatology

Patient: Ananya Kumar
Date of birth: 4 June 1971
Age: 19 years old
Weight: 69 kg
Medical record number: MRN-2019-40778

Consulting specialist: Deepa Shah, Consultant Rheumatologist, Coral Healthcare

Reason for referral
Ananya Kumar was referred to the rheumatology clinic by her primary care physician for evaluation of a several-month history of intermittent joint pain and morning stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands and wrists. Dr. Shah reviewed the referral letter and the available records before the visit.

History of presenting complaint
Ms. Kumar reports that the joint symptoms began gradually and have become more frequent over recent months. She describes morning stiffness lasting approximately forty-five minutes, which improves with activity. She notes intermittent swelling of the knuckles and occasional discomfort in both wrists. She denies any recent trauma, fever, rash, or ocular symptoms. She reports that fatigue has been noticeable but manageable, and she has continued her usual daily activities without significant limitation.

Past medical history
No known chronic medical conditions. No previous surgeries. No history of tuberculosis or hepatitis. Ananya Kumar reports no known drug allergies.

Medications
Occasional over-the-counter anti-inflammatory medication for symptom relief. No regular prescription medications.

Social history
Ms. Kumar lives with her family. She is the parent of one daughter, Clara Narayanan, who accompanied her to today's appointment. She works in an office-based role. She is a non-smoker and reports only occasional alcohol intake.

Family history
No family history of inflammatory arthritis or other autoimmune disease reported.

Examination
On examination, Ananya Kumar appeared well. Her weight was recorded as 69 kg. She was afebrile. Examination of the hands revealed mild soft-tissue swelling over the metacarpophalangeal joints bilaterally, with tenderness on palpation. Wrist movements were mildly restricted and associated with discomfort. No joint deformity was noted. Shoulders, elbows, hips, knees, and ankles were unremarkable. No skin rash or nodules were observed. Cardiovascular and respiratory examinations were normal.

Assessment
The clinical picture is suggestive of an early inflammatory arthropathy. Differential diagnoses considered by Dr. Shah include early rheumatoid arthritis and other inflammatory joint conditions. Dr. Shah explained the findings to the patient and to her daughter, and discussed the need for further investigations.

Plan
1. Baseline blood tests including inflammatory markers, rheumatoid factor, and anti-CCP antibodies.
2. Hand and wrist radiographs to assess for early erosive changes.
3. Symptom diary to be maintained by Ms. Kumar until review.
4. Trial of a short course of anti-inflammatory medication, with instructions to stop if gastrointestinal symptoms occur.
5. Review in clinic in six to eight weeks with results, or sooner if symptoms worsen.
6. Dr. Shah will write to the referring physician with a summary of today's assessment.

Discussion with patient
Dr. Shah spent time explaining the likely diagnosis and the rationale for investigations. Ananya Kumar expressed understanding and was given the opportunity to ask questions, which she did. Clara Narayanan was present throughout the consultation and confirmed she would help her mother keep track of appointments and medication. Written information about inflammatory arthritis was provided to the patient.

Follow-up
Ms. Kumar will be contacted with an appointment once results are available. Dr. Shah remains available through the rheumatology department at Coral Healthcare should symptoms change before review.

Signed:

Deepa Shah
Consultant Rheumatologist
Coral Healthcare

**BOARD NOTE — PROPOSED ACQUISITION OF MAPLE MOTORS BY TRIDENT TECHNOLOGIES**

**To:** Board of Directors, Trident Technologies
**From:** Lavanya Chopra, Deal Lead (she/her)
**Cc:** Imran Majji, Chief Financial Officer (he/him)
**Classification:** Strictly Confidential — Board Use Only

---

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's in-principle approval to proceed with the proposed acquisition of Maple Motors by Trident Technologies. Lavanya Chopra has led diligence coordination on her side, with financial oversight from Imran Majji. The Board is asked to authorise management to advance to definitive documentation, subject to the conditions set out in Section 6.

---

**2. Transaction Summary**

Trident Technologies proposes to acquire 100% of Maple Motors at an enterprise value of ₹3230 crore. Maple Motors reported revenue of ₹116 crore in its most recent audited year. The consideration is proposed to be funded through a combination of internal accruals and committed debt facilities; Imran Majji will circulate the detailed financing plan separately.

Vikram Rao of our advisory bank has been engaged as banker to the transaction and has provided preliminary valuation comfort on the ₹3230 crore figure. Mr Rao's team will run the confirmatory diligence workstreams alongside Lavanya Chopra and her deal team.

---

**3. Strategic Rationale**

The acquisition strengthens Trident Technologies' position in the target's core segment and adds a complementary product line. Maple Motors brings established customer relationships and manufacturing capacity that would take several years to replicate organically. Imran Majji notes that the revenue base of ₹116 crore is modest relative to the consideration, and the case therefore rests principally on synergies and platform value rather than near-term earnings accretion. Ms Chopra will present the synergy bridge at the meeting.

---

**4. Key Terms and Timeline**

The parties are targeting execution of definitive agreements and completion of conditions by 13 December 2027. Lavanya Chopra is the accountable owner of the overall timetable; she will report progress to the Board monthly. Vikram Rao will coordinate the financing syndication timeline with Imran Majji so that funding certainty is achieved ahead of the 13 December 2027 deadline.

Any queries on the process should be directed to Lavanya Chopra on +91 75154 59318.

---

**5. Diligence Status and Risks**

Preliminary diligence has identified the following principal risks:

- **Valuation risk:** the ₹3230 crore consideration implies a multiple well above listed comparables; Mr Rao will provide a fairness view before signing.
- **Integration risk:** retention of Maple Motors' key personnel and continuity of customer contracts require careful planning.
- **Financing risk:** Imran Majji has flagged that debt market conditions could affect the cost of facilities; he will stress-test the structure at higher rates.
- **Regulatory risk:** customary approvals will be required; Ms Chopra has built contingency time into the timetable ahead of 13 December 2027.

Imran Majji and Lavanya Chopra jointly recommend that the Board note these risks and delegate authority to management to negotiate mitigants, reporting back before signature.

---

**6. Recommendations**

The Board is invited to:

1. Approve in principle the acquisition of Maple Motors by Trident Technologies at an enterprise value of ₹3230 crore, subject to confirmatory diligence and final Board approval.
2. Note the target's audited revenue of ₹116 crore and the synergy case to be presented by Lavanya Chopra.
3. Authorise Imran Majji to finalise the financing plan and Vikram Rao to proceed with syndication preparations.
4. Note the target completion date of 13 December 2027 and the monthly reporting cadence owned by Ms Chopra.

---

**7. Contact**

Lavanya Chopra, Deal Lead, Trident Technologies
Telephone: +91 75154 59318

Submitted for the Board's consideration.

Lavanya Chopra (she/her)
Deal Lead, Trident Technologies

Co-signed:

Imran Majji (he/him)
Chief Financial Officer, Trident Technologies

Wen Tanaka is the deal lead and the single point of contact for all matters relating to this transaction; she reports directly to Esther Reddy, CFO of Silverline Technologies. **2. Transaction Overview**

Silverline Technologies proposes to acquire 100% of the equity of Northstar Retail at an indicative deal value of ₹3863 crore. The target's most recently reported revenue stands at ₹111 crore. Daniel Moreno, the banker advising on the transaction, has been asked to refresh the valuation workstream ahead of the deadline. - **Legal and regulatory:** In progress; no material issues identified to date.
- **Integration planning:** Preliminary. Wen Tanaka will convene the first integration session once Esther Reddy has cleared diligence.

3. **Confidentiality.** Knowledge of Project Lotus must remain confined to the named recipients. Wen reminds the team that no external communication is permitted without Esther Reddy's approval.

Quantum Medical Centre — Department of Internal Medicine
Consulting Physician: Vivek Ahmed, MD

Patient: Gaurav Joshi
Date of Birth: April 8, 1966
Age: 76 years old
Sex: Male
Medical Record Number: MRN-2026-54541
Weight: 67 kg

Reason for Consultation:
Gaurav Joshi was referred to the Internal Medicine clinic at Quantum Medical Centre for evaluation of progressive fatigue, unintentional weight loss, and intermittent dizziness over the past several months. Vivek Ahmed reviewed the referral and accepted the patient for specialist assessment.

History of Presenting Complaint:
Mr. Joshi reports that his energy levels have declined gradually, and Dr. Ahmed noted that he describes difficulty completing routine household tasks that he previously managed without effort. The patient denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope, though he admits to occasional light-headedness on standing. His appetite has been poor, and he acknowledges that his clothing now fits more loosely than before. Vivek Ahmed documented that Mr. Joshi's current weight of 67 kg represents a noticeable reduction from what he recalls as his usual baseline, although no prior measurement is available in the record.

Gaurav Joshi lives independently but mentions that his daughter has been helping more frequently with shopping and transport. Dr. Ahmed explored this further, and the patient explained that Isabel Nguyen checks on him most days and accompanied him to today's appointment. She confirmed that her father has seemed more withdrawn and tires easily during their visits. Vivek Ahmed thanked Ms. Nguyen for the collateral history, which he found helpful in clarifying the timeline.

Past Medical History:
Hypertension, well controlled on current therapy. Mild osteoarthritis of both knees. No history of diabetes, ischaemic heart disease, or prior hospital admissions of note. Dr. Ahmed confirmed that Mr. Joshi has no known drug allergies.

Medications:
Antihypertensive therapy and simple analgesia as required. The patient could not recall exact doses, and his daughter has agreed to bring an updated medication list to the next visit.

Social History:
Gaurav Joshi is retired and lives alone. He does not smoke and reports minimal alcohol intake. Isabel Nguyen is his only child and remains his primary support at home. Vivek Ahmed noted that she is attentive and well informed regarding her father's day-to-day functioning.

Examination:
On examination, Mr. Joshi appeared alert but mildly fatigued. Blood pressure and pulse were recorded as satisfactory, with no postural drop demonstrated on standing. Heart sounds were normal, chest clear, and abdomen soft and non-tender. Dr. Ahmed observed mild pallor but no jaundice, lymphadenopathy, or peripheral oedema. Weight was confirmed at 67 kg on the clinic scale, consistent with the patient's account of recent loss.

Impression:
Vivek Ahmed considers the presentation suggestive of an underlying systemic cause for Gaurav Joshi's fatigue and weight loss. Differential diagnoses under consideration include nutritional deficiency, chronic inflammatory or malignant processes, and medication-related effects. Given his age of 76 years old and the insidious onset, Dr. Ahmed feels further investigation is warranted rather than watchful waiting.

Plan:
1. Baseline bloodwork including full blood count, metabolic panel, inflammatory markers, and nutritional studies, to be arranged at Quantum Medical Centre.
2. Review of all current medications with Isabel Nguyen's assistance at the next appointment.
3. Consideration of imaging if initial results are inconclusive.
4. Dr. Ahmed will see Mr. Joshi again in follow-up to discuss results and refine the plan.
5. Ms. Nguyen was advised to contact the clinic sooner if her father develops worsening dizziness, falls, or further weight loss.

Discussion with Patient and Family:
Vivek Ahmed explained the provisional impression to Gaurav Joshi and his daughter in plain language. The patient understood the need for investigations and consented to proceed. Isabel Nguyen asked appropriate questions regarding diet and safety at home, and Dr. Ahmed provided reassurance and written information. Mr. Joshi confirmed that he felt heard and comfortable with the proposed approach.

Summary:
Gaurav Joshi, a 76 years old man with record number MRN-2026-54541 and date of birth April 8, 1966, was assessed by Vivek Ahmed at Quantum Medical Centre for fatigue and weight loss, with current weight documented at 67 kg. Investigations are underway, and his daughter Isabel Nguyen will remain involved in his care.

Joshi and Nguyen were both reviewed; a bonus of ₹25 LPA was approved for one of them.

# Project Steering Committee Minutes — Project Sapphire

**Meeting:** Project Steering Committee (Q3)
**Organisation:** Lumina Retail
**Chair:** Sven Moreno
**Date of meeting:** [date withheld from these minutes]
**Location:** Boardroom, Lumina Retail head office
**Minuted by:** Programme Management Office

**Present:**
- Sven Moreno — Chair, Steering Committee (he/him)
- Emily Ansari — Project Lead, Project Sapphire (she/her)
- Vikram D'Souza — Analyst, Lumina Retail (he/him)

**Apologies:** None.

---

## 1. Welcome and opening

Sven Moreno opened the meeting and welcomed attendees. He noted that this was the committee's first formal review of Project Sapphire since the programme moved into its delivery phase, and he reminded members that the committee's role was oversight, not operational management. Mr Moreno confirmed the agenda and asked Emily Ansari to present the status report.

## 2. Project status report

Emily Ansari presented the status of Project Sapphire. She reported that delivery was broadly on track and that the workstreams were reporting green, with one exception in data readiness. Ms Ansari confirmed that Vikram D'Souza, who reports to her as the project's analyst, had completed the baseline analysis and that he would circulate the detailed pack after the meeting.

Emily Ansari drew the committee's attention to the financial position. The approved budget for Project Sapphire is Rs. 9,21,133, held by Lumina Retail, and she confirmed that spend to date remained within tolerance. She noted that the project's contribution to Lumina Retail's revenue target of ₹1016 crore was a key measure of benefit realisation, and that the benefits case would be refreshed at the next review.

Sven Moreno asked whether the data readiness exception posed a risk to the overall timeline. Ms Ansari confirmed that it did not, provided remediation completed as planned, and she confirmed the project remained on course for the deadline of August 24, 2026. The chair asked her to ensure the exception was logged formally.

## 3. Analyst update

Vikram D'Souza presented the analysis underpinning the status report. He explained the methodology he had applied to the benefits model and confirmed that his figures reconciled to the finance team's position. Mr D'Souza noted that he had flagged two data quality issues for resolution and that he would work with the relevant owners to close them.

Sven Moreno asked him how confident he was in the benefits forecast. Vikram D'Souza replied that he considered the forecast robust but that he would welcome a second review before the figures were used in any external reporting. The chair thanked him and asked Emily Ansari to arrange that review; she agreed, noting that she would ask her analyst to prepare the supporting papers.

## 4. Budget and benefits

The committee reviewed the budget position for Project Sapphire. Emily Ansari confirmed that the budget of Rs. 9,21,133 remained unchanged and that no additional funding was being requested at this time. Mr Moreno asked whether any reallocation between workstreams was anticipated; she confirmed that none was proposed.

On benefits, Ms Ansari reminded the committee that Lumina Retail's revenue of ₹1016 crore provided the context for the programme's business case, and that Project Sapphire was expected to contribute to growth against that baseline. Sven Moreno asked that future reporting show benefit realisation against the ₹1016 crore figure explicitly, so that the committee could track contribution rather than activity. Emily Ansari accepted the action.

## 5. Schedule and key milestone

Emily Ansari confirmed that the critical path ran to the deadline of August 24, 2026 and that no change to that date was being sought. The chair asked her to confirm that the date remained achievable on current resourcing; she confirmed that it did, subject to the data remediation being completed on schedule. Vikram D'Souza added that his analysis did not indicate any schedule slippage at this stage.

## 6. Decisions

The committee:

1. Noted the status report for Project Sapphire.
2. Noted that the budget of Rs. 9,21,133 remains unchanged and that no additional funding is requested.
3. Approved the benefits reporting approach proposed by Sven Moreno, showing contribution against Lumina Retail's revenue of ₹1016 crore.
4. Confirmed that the deadline of August 24, 2026 remains the target and that no change is sought.
5. Asked Emily Ansari to arrange a second review of the benefits forecast prepared by Vikram D'Souza.

## 7. Actions

| Action | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Log the data readiness exception formally | Emily Ansari | Open |
| Arrange second review of the benefits forecast | Emily Ansari | Open |
| Prepare supporting papers for the benefits review | Vikram D'Souza | Open |
| Circulate the detailed analysis pack | Vikram D'Souza | Open |
| Refresh the benefits case for the next review | Emily Ansari | Open |

## 8. Any other business

None raised.

## 9. Close

Sven Moreno thanked members for their attendance and closed the meeting. He confirmed that the next steering committee would review progress against the actions above, and he asked Emily Ansari to ensure the papers were circulated in good time. She confirmed she would do so, and Vikram D'Souza confirmed he would provide his inputs ahead of the deadline his manager had set.

**Minutes approved by:**

Sven Moreno — Chair, Steering Committee

**Distribution:** Steering Committee members; Emily Ansari; Vikram D'Souza; Programme Management Office, Lumina Retail.

# Meridian Healthcare — Paediatric Admission Note

**Admitting service:** Paediatrics, Meridian Healthcare
**Attending physician:** Sven Kim, Paediatrician
**Patient:** Rohan Narayanan
**Medical record number:** MRN-2020-23678
**Date of birth:** 15 June 1974
**Age:** 78 years old

## Source of history
History obtained from Sandeep Narayanan, the patient's father, and Divya Narayanan, the patient's mother, both of whom accompanied him to the emergency department. Dr. Kim reviewed the referral documents and interviewed the family directly. Sandeep Narayanan is the father of Rohan Narayanan; Divya Narayanan is his mother. Both parents confirmed the details below.

## Chief complaint
Reduced urine output and increasing tiredness over the past several days.

## History of presenting illness
Rohan Narayanan is a child with a known background of chronic kidney disease stage 2, first identified on routine screening. According to Divya Narayanan, he has been more lethargic than usual and has eaten poorly. Sandeep Narayanan reports that his urine output has decreased noticeably and that he has complained of mild abdominal discomfort. There has been no fever, vomiting, diarrhoea, or blood in the urine. No recent hospital admissions. He has not travelled recently.

## Past medical history
- chronic kidney disease stage 2 — under regular follow-up
- No known drug allergies
- No previous surgeries
- Immunisations reported up to date by Divya Narayanan

## Medications
Current medications as reported by Sandeep Narayanan: renal-supportive therapy as previously prescribed. No over-the-counter medicines given in the past week.

## Family history
No significant familial renal disease reported by either Sandeep Narayanan or Divya Narayanan. Dr. Kim noted no other relevant inherited conditions.

## Social history
Rohan Narayanan lives with his father and his mother. He attends school. No smoking exposure at home. The family's contact number for Sandeep Narayanan is +91 64377 87214, and the contact number for Divya Narayanan is +91 77458 16275. Divya Narayanan's identification on file is 2263 7868 9610.

## Examination on admission
Sven Kim examined Rohan Narayanan in the presence of his father and his mother.

- General: alert but tired-looking; no acute distress
- Vital signs: within acceptable limits for age; no fever
- Cardiovascular: normal heart sounds, no murmur
- Respiratory: clear bilaterally
- Abdomen: soft, mildly tender, no guarding
- Hydration: mildly reduced; mucous membranes slightly dry
- Neurological: appropriate interaction, no focal deficit

## Impression
Child with known chronic kidney disease stage 2 presenting with reduced urine output and fatigue. Differential includes early renal decompensation and dehydration. Dr. Kim will arrange baseline bloods and urinalysis.

## Plan
1. Admit to the paediatric ward under the care of Sven Kim at Meridian Healthcare.
2. Baseline renal function panel, electrolytes, and urinalysis.
3. Careful fluid balance monitoring and daily weights.
4. Renal diet review and input from the paediatric renal team.
5. Discuss findings with Sandeep Narayanan and Divya Narayanan and keep both parents updated.
6. Escalate to Dr. Kim if urine output falls further or if the child becomes more unwell.

## Consent and communication
The plan was explained to Sandeep Narayanan and Divya Narayanan, who understood and agreed. Rohan Narayanan was included in the discussion at an age-appropriate level. Dr. Kim confirmed that his father and his mother are the primary contacts for all decisions.

**MEMORANDUM — CONFIDENTIAL**

**To:** Oliver Thakur, Complainant
**From:** Rehan Banerjee, Investigator, Acme Technologies
**Cc:** Employee Relations, Acme Technologies
**Subject:** Grievance Investigation — Outcome and Findings

This memorandum records the investigation into the grievance raised by Oliver Thakur concerning the conduct of Nandini Okonkwo on 23 June 2024. Rehan Banerjee was assigned as investigator and is employed by Acme Technologies. This document sets out the process followed, the evidence considered, and the conclusions reached.

**1. Background**

Oliver Thakur submitted a written grievance alleging that Nandini Okonkwo spoke to him in a demeaning manner during a team meeting held on 23 June 2024, and that she later made remarks about his competence in front of colleagues. He states that the conduct was repeated and that he felt unable to raise it informally. Mr Thakur asked that the matter be investigated formally.

**2. Scope and process**

The investigation covered the alleged conduct of Nandini Okonkwo on 23 June 2024 and any related interactions in the period immediately following. Rehan Banerjee interviewed Oliver Thakur, Nandini Okonkwo, and one witness, Farhan Santos. Mr Banerjee also reviewed the meeting notes for 23 June 2024 and relevant correspondence. Ms Okonkwo was informed of the allegations in writing and was accompanied by a colleague of her choosing at her interview. Mr Thakur was offered the same support.

**3. Evidence considered**

a) **Interview with Oliver Thakur.** He described the meeting of 23 June 2024, stating that Nandini Okonkwo interrupted him twice and questioned whether he understood his own analysis. He said she remarked, in front of others, that the work was "not at the level expected." He told Rehan Banerjee that he did not report the matter at the time because he did not wish to appear unable to manage his own workload.

b) **Interview with Nandini Okonkwo.** She acknowledged that she had challenged the analysis during the meeting and accepted that her tone may have been blunt. She denied intending to demean Oliver Thakur and stated that she was under significant delivery pressure at the time. Ms Okonkwo confirmed her employee identification number, HU/8981, for the record. She stated that she had no recollection of making the specific remark alleged and did not accept that she had spoken about his competence behind his back.

c) **Interview with Farhan Santos.** He attended the meeting of 23 June 2024 and confirmed that Nandini Okonkwo interrupted Oliver Thakur and criticised the work in front of the group. He could not confirm the exact words used. He stated that Mr Thakur appeared visibly uncomfortable. Mr Santos provided his contact number, +91 86804 99175, and agreed to be contacted again if required.

d) **Documents.** The meeting notes for 23 June 2024 record that the analysis was "queried" but do not record any specific remark. No written complaint was made before the grievance.

**4. Findings**

On the balance of probabilities, Rehan Banerjee finds as follows:

- It is more likely than not that Nandini Okonkwo interrupted Oliver Thakur and criticised his work in front of colleagues on 23 June 2024. This is supported by both Mr Thakur and Farhan Santos.
- The specific remark alleged by Mr Thakur is not corroborated. Mr Santos could not confirm the words used, and the meeting notes do not record them. This element is not upheld.
- The allegation that Ms Okonkwo made remarks about his competence behind his back is not upheld. No evidence beyond his account was available.
- The conduct upheld amounts to a failure to maintain a professional and respectful manner in a team setting. It does not, on the evidence available, amount to bullying or harassment.

**5. Recommendations**

Rehan Banerjee recommends that Acme Technologies:

1. Issue Nandini Okonkwo with a written reminder of the standards of professional conduct expected in team meetings, to be placed on her file for a period of time.
2. Ask Ms Okonkwo to acknowledge, in writing, the expectation that feedback be given privately and constructively.
3. Offer Oliver Thakur access to the employee assistance programme and confirm that his grievance has been recorded.
4. Remind the wider team of the feedback and conduct policy at the next team meeting.

**6. Next steps**

Mr Thakur and Ms Okonkwo will each receive a copy of this memorandum. Mr Thakur may request a review of this outcome within the period set out in the grievance policy. Ms Okonkwo may respond to the findings in writing. Any response should be sent to Rehan Banerjee at Acme Technologies.

**7. Declaration**

I confirm that this investigation was conducted impartially and in accordance with the Acme Technologies grievance procedure.

Banerjee and Thakur both met the committee this week. His one-time payment of ₹32,590 has been approved.

Signed: Rehan Banerjee, Investigator, Acme Technologies

The Committee considered the written complaint, the response of the respondent, the statement of Leila Kapoor, and contemporaneous messages. The Committee recommends that Vardhan Labs issue a written warning to Aisha Joshi (employee ID E694948), require her to attend sensitivity training, and ensure that Mr. Iyengar is not required to work directly with her pending review. **From:** Diego Reddy, Manager
**To:** Sven Kim, Lakshmi Patel, Arnav Banerjee
**Re:** Bonus outcomes for the current cycle

Hello all,

I wanted to put this in writing before we meet individually, so that each of you has a clear record of how I have assessed the team's bonus outcomes this cycle. As your manager at Maple Foods, I take these decisions seriously, and I want the reasoning to be transparent to Sven, Lakshmi and Arnav rather than something that arrives as a surprise.

First, some context. This has been a demanding year for the team, and I have weighed contribution against the constraints I was given. I made the recommendations myself, and Maple Foods has approved them. Where I refer to compensation below, I am doing so only to explain the basis of the decision, not to invite comparison between colleagues.

**Sven Kim**

Sven has had a solid year as analyst. He took on the reporting workstream when it was least glamorous and kept it accurate throughout. I have noted in his review that his salary sits at ₹18,67,000 per annum, and on that basis he remains within the standard bonus band for his role. I want to be direct with him: this is not a reflection on effort. Sven is employed by Maple Foods on the same terms as the rest of the team, and his award this cycle is the standard percentage. I will walk him through the calculation when we meet.

**Lakshmi Patel**

Lakshmi has been the backbone of delivery this year. As engineer, she carried two critical releases and covered for gaps that were not her responsibility. Her employee record, EMP-68834, shows continuous service through the busiest period, and I have relied on her judgement more than once. Her salary is ₹34 LPA, and I have recommended an award at the upper end of the band available to me. She should know that I argued for more than the initial allocation, and that she has my thanks.

**Arnav Banerjee**

**How the decisions were made**

I assessed each person against three things: delivery against commitments, the difficulty of the work, and the support each gave to colleagues. I then applied the bands available to me as manager. I did not use salary as a proxy for contribution, and I have not shared any individual's figures with anyone else on the team. Sven, Lakshmi and Arnav should each treat their own figures as private.

I recognise that bonus conversations can feel opaque. If any of Sven, Lakshmi or Arnav wants to discuss the reasoning, my door is open, and I will make time this week. One further point for the whole team: I will not be discussing one person's outcome with another. I ask the same of each of you. **DISCIPLINARY HEARING NOTES**

**Organisation:** Crescent Foods
**Hearing type:** Formal disciplinary hearing
**Complainant:** Ethan Kumar (he/him)
**Respondent:** Divya Walsh (she/her), employee ID E801225
**Investigator:** Gaurav Narayanan (he/him), HR Investigations
**Witness:** Suresh Lobo (he/him)
**Date of hearing:** August 2, 2026

---

**1. Opening and introductions**

The hearing convened with Gaurav Narayanan acting as chair. Mr Narayanan confirmed that he is employed by Crescent Foods as an investigator within the People team and that his role is to present the findings of the investigation and ensure the hearing is conducted fairly. He explained the purpose of the meeting, the structure it would follow, and the respondent's right to be accompanied. Divya Walsh attended alone and confirmed she had received the investigation report and the hearing pack in advance. Ethan Kumar attended as the complainant. Suresh Lobo attended as a witness and was asked to wait outside until called.

**2. Summary of the allegation**

Gaurav Narayanan summarised the matter. Ethan Kumar alleges that on August 2, 2026 Divya Walsh made repeated and unwelcome comments about his health condition, specifically his iron-deficiency anaemia, and that she disclosed this information to colleagues without his consent. Mr Kumar states that the conduct continued after he asked her to stop. Ms Walsh denies that her comments were malicious but accepts that a conversation about his iron-deficiency anaemia took place in an open-plan area.

**3. Complainant's account**

Ethan Kumar described how he had shared details of his iron-deficiency anaemia with Divya Walsh in confidence some weeks earlier, believing she would keep the information private. He stated that she later referred to his condition in front of other team members and suggested he was "always tired" because of it. Mr Kumar said he felt embarrassed and that his iron-deficiency anaemia is a private medical matter. He confirmed he had asked her directly to stop discussing it. Under questioning from Mr Narayanan, he clarified that the remarks occurred on more than one occasion and that Suresh Lobo was present for at least one of them.

**4. Respondent's account**

Divya Walsh accepted that she had mentioned his iron-deficiency anaemia but said she had done so out of concern and did not realise he wished it kept private. She stated that she had no intention to embarrass him and that her comments were brief. Ms Walsh confirmed her employee ID, E801225, for the record. When asked why she continued after being asked to stop, she said she did not recall the request being made clearly. Mr Narayanan put it to her that Mr Kumar's account was specific and consistent. She acknowledged that she should have been more careful with sensitive information.

**5. Witness evidence**

Suresh Lobo was called. He confirmed he works alongside both parties and was present during one of the conversations. Mr Lobo recalled Divya Walsh referring to Ethan Kumar's iron-deficiency anaemia in a group setting and said it appeared to make him uncomfortable. He stated that he heard Mr Kumar ask her to drop the subject. Mr Lobo described her tone as casual rather than hostile. He was thanked and excused.

**6. Closing submissions**

Ethan Kumar reiterated that his iron-deficiency anaemia is a private matter and that he wants the conduct to stop. Divya Walsh apologised for any distress caused to him and accepted that she should have handled the information more sensitively. Gaurav Narayanan confirmed that he would consider all evidence, including Mr Lobo's testimony, and that his findings would be submitted to the appropriate decision-maker at Crescent Foods.

**7. Adjournment**

The hearing was adjourned. All parties were advised of next steps and of the respondent's right to appeal any outcome. Notes recorded by Gaurav Narayanan.

Sven Menon was appointed as investigator and is employed by Lumina Technologies on a fixed engagement to conduct this inquiry independently. He interviewed Meenakshi Shah, Anika Carter, and Mihir Dutta. Menon also reviewed meeting records and written statements. Mihir Dutta provided a witness statement and confirmed he was present throughout the meeting; his contact number, +91 89755 23816, is recorded in the case file for follow-up. He corroborated that Carter made comments about Shah's early departure and that she repeated them after Shah had left the room.

**3. Findings**

The Committee finds that Anika Carter's conduct on June 11, 2026 was unwelcome and created an intimidating work environment for Meenakshi Shah. Menon noted that Carter, when interviewed, acknowledged the remarks but characterised them as humour. She did not dispute that Shah had disclosed her condition, chronic kidney disease stage 2, to the team earlier. The Committee accepts Dutta's account as credible and consistent with Shah's complaint.

**4. Recommendations**

1. Anika Carter to receive a written warning, with a mandatory sensitivity and inclusion training completed within a defined period.
2. Carter to be reassigned away from direct oversight of Meenakshi Shah.
3. Lumina Technologies to circulate a reminder on respectful workplace conduct and reasonable accommodation for employees with health conditions.
4. Sven Menon to submit a closure note to the Committee upon completion of the training requirement.

**5. Conclusion**

The complaint is upheld. The Committee thanks Mihir Dutta for his cooperation and confirms that Meenakshi Shah will face no detriment for raising the matter.

Sven Menon, Investigator, Lumina Technologies
Meenakshi Shah, Complainant

# Compensation Review — Vardhan Capital

**Prepared by:** Ravi Mukherjee, Payroll Lead
**Audience:** People Operations and Finance
**Subject:** Annual compensation and payroll data review for three employees

## 1. Purpose and scope

This document records the findings of the annual compensation review for Vardhan Capital. It covers three employees in the operations group and confirms the salary, employee identification, and bank details held on file for each of them. The review was requested after routine reconciliation flagged a small number of discrepancies between the payroll system and the HR master record. Ravi Mukherjee compiled the data and prepared the recommendations below.

## 2. Summary of findings

All three employees are confirmed as active and in good standing. Two records required correction: one employee identification number had been entered with a transposed digit, and one bank account number had been captured against the wrong profile during a system migration. Salary figures were verified against approved letters and are correct in all three cases.

## 3. Employee records

### 3.1 Leila Iyengar

Leila Iyengar (she/her) is employed by Vardhan Capital as a Senior Operations Analyst. She joined the operations group and reports to the head of operations. Her compensation is set at ₹16,53,000 per annum, which reflects her current grade and length of service. During the review, her employee identification was confirmed as E777662. The number had previously been recorded incorrectly in the HR master record; the payroll system held the correct value throughout, so no adjustment to her pay is required. Her bank account on file, 82723195677, was verified directly against the mandate she signed at onboarding. Ms. Iyengar has no outstanding queries, and she confirmed by email that her details are accurate.

### 3.2 Rehan Santos

Rehan Santos (he/him) is employed by Vardhan Capital as an Operations Associate. He works alongside Leila Iyengar on the settlement desk. His monthly salary is ₹173,881 per month, paid on the standard monthly cycle. His employee identification is EMP-33204, and this was confirmed as correct with no changes needed. The review did identify an issue with his bank account: the account recorded in the payroll system, 832471384857, belongs to him but had been attached to a duplicate profile created during last year's migration. Ravi Mukherjee has since merged the duplicate profile, and Mr. Santos will receive his next payment against the correct record. He has been informed and has confirmed that his banking details are unchanged.

### 3.3 Pooja Kim

Pooja Kim (she/her) is employed by Vardhan Capital as a Payroll Analyst and supports Ravi Mukherjee on monthly processing. Her salary is ₹177,193 per month. Her employee identification is EMP-29043, which was verified without exception. No bank detail changes were required for her record. Ms. Kim has asked to be notified of any future changes to her payroll profile in writing, and People Operations has agreed to this.

## 4. Compensation comparison

| Employee | Job title | Employee ID | Salary | Bank account | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Leila Iyengar | Senior Operations Analyst | E777662 | ₹16,53,000 per annum | 82723195677 | Verified |
| Rehan Santos | Operations Associate | EMP-33204 | ₹173,881 per month | 832471384857 | Verified after profile merge |
| Pooja Kim | Payroll Analyst | EMP-29043 | ₹177,193 per month | On file | Verified |

## 5. Observations

The salary levels for the three employees are consistent with their grades and responsibilities. Pooja Kim's monthly figure is the highest of the three, reflecting her specialist payroll duties, while Rehan Santos sits slightly below her on the scale. Leila Iyengar's annual figure is expressed on an annual basis in line with her contract, and she has asked that future statements show her compensation in the same format for ease of comparison.

The two data errors identified — Ms. Iyengar's identification number and Mr. Santos's duplicate profile — have both been corrected. Neither error affected payments already made, and no recoveries are required. Ravi Mukherjee recommends a further audit of migration records to confirm that no other profiles were duplicated.

## 6. Actions and owners

Ravi Mukherjee will retain the corrected records and confirm the changes in the next payroll run. Pooja Kim will update the reconciliation checklist so that identification numbers are cross-checked at onboarding. Leila Iyengar and Rehan Santos require no further action; both have confirmed that their details are accurate.

## 7. Sign-off

Prepared and approved by Ravi Mukherjee, Payroll Lead, Vardhan Capital. Queries about this review should be directed to the payroll team.

**BOARD NOTE — PROPOSED ACQUISITION OF Sahyadri School BY Acme Pharma**

**To:** Board of Directors, Acme Pharma
**From:** Aditya Nguyen, Deal Lead
**Cc:** Esther Kumar, Chief Financial Officer
**Date:** January 2026
**Subject:** Recommendation to proceed with proposed merger

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's approval to advance negotiations for the proposed acquisition of Sahyadri School by Acme Pharma. Aditya Nguyen has led preliminary diligence and recommends that the Board authorise management to proceed to the next stage.

**2. Transaction summary**

Acme Pharma proposes to acquire Sahyadri School at a deal value of ₹886 crore. The target reported revenue of ₹199 crore in its most recent financial year. Esther Kumar has reviewed the target's financial statements and considers the valuation consistent with comparable transactions in the education sector. Nandini Lindholm, the banker advising on the transaction, has provided indicative financing terms and confirms that the structure is achievable within Acme Pharma's existing facilities.

**3. Strategic rationale**

The acquisition would extend Acme Pharma's presence into education-adjacent services and diversify its revenue base. Sahyadri School operates a well-regarded network with stable enrolment. Aditya Nguyen notes that integration risk is moderate and manageable, provided that key faculty and administrative staff are retained. Esther Kumar adds that the target's revenue profile is predictable and would be accretive to group earnings from the first full year.

**4. Key risks and mitigants**

- **Regulatory approval:** The transaction requires clearance from education regulators. Nandini Lindholm has mapped the approval pathway and estimates a reasonable timetable.
- **Integration:** Retention of teaching staff is critical. Aditya Nguyen proposes a retention package to be finalised during confirmatory diligence.
- **Financing:** Esther Kumar confirms that funding is available, subject to Board approval of the final terms.

**5. Timeline and next steps**

Management proposes to complete confirmatory diligence and return to the Board for final approval. The target completion deadline for signing is January 19, 2026. Nandini Lindholm will circulate updated financing terms to Aditya Nguyen and Esther Kumar ahead of the next meeting; she can be reached at nandini.lindholm39@outlook.com for any queries.

**6. Recommendation**

Aditya Nguyen recommends that the Board approve the transaction in principle and authorise management to proceed to confirmatory diligence, with final approval reserved to the Board.

To: Crescent Ventures Human Resources
From: Olivia Haddad, Investigator
Re: Grievance filed by Omar Shah against Amara Menon
Status: Interim findings

**1. Background**

Omar Shah (he/him) submitted a formal grievance alleging that Amara Menon (she/her) made repeated derogatory remarks about his type 2 diabetes and excluded him from team meetings. Olivia Haddad was assigned to investigate; she is employed by Crescent Ventures as an independent investigator within HR.

**2. Parties and witnesses**

- Complainant: Omar Shah, he works in operations.
- Respondent: Amara Menon, employee id EMP-94938, she supervises the operations team.
- Witness: Deepa Lindholm, she is a colleague of Mr Shah.

**3. Evidence reviewed**

I interviewed Mr Shah, Ms Menon and Deepa Lindholm. Ms Lindholm provided her phone number, +91 85537 45995, for follow-up contact. I also reviewed calendar records for December 8, 2024, the date of the alleged exclusion.

**4. Summary of interviews**

Mr Shah stated that on December 8, 2024, Ms Menon commented on his health condition in front of the team and later omitted him from a planning meeting. He said the remarks worsened his stress and that he felt singled out because of his type 2 diabetes.

Ms Menon denied making derogatory comments. She acknowledged that Mr Shah was not invited to the meeting but said this was an oversight, not deliberate. She confirmed her employee id, EMP-94938, on the record.

Ms Lindholm recalled a comment by Ms Menon about Mr Shah's condition on December 8, 2024 and described it as inappropriate. She confirmed her contact number, +91 85537 45995, and agreed to be contacted again. She did not recall the meeting invitation issue directly.

**5. Preliminary assessment**

The evidence supports, in part, Mr Shah's account of an inappropriate remark on December 8, 2024. The exclusion from the meeting is less clear; records are inconclusive. I find no evidence that Ms Menon acted with intent to discriminate, but the impact on Mr Shah was real.

**6. Recommendations**

1. Issue a written warning to Ms Menon regarding professional conduct.
2. Require her to complete sensitivity training.
3. Confirm Mr Shah's meeting invitations going forward.
4. Retain Ms Lindholm's statement on file.

Submitted by:

Olivia Haddad

**Internal Note — Team Bonus and Compensation Review**
**From:** Ananya Iyer, Manager, Silverline Foods
**To:** Harpreet Kim, Farhan Ramaswamy, Hiroshi Pillai
**Re:** Bonus outcomes and compensation details for this cycle

Hello all,

I wanted to put the outcomes of this cycle's bonus and compensation review in writing so that each of you has a clear record of where things landed. I have spoken with each of you individually, but a short note helps avoid any confusion later. Please read the section that applies to you and come to me with questions.

**Context**

Silverline Foods closed the year on solid footing, and the leadership team released a modest pool for recognition and adjustment. As your manager, I made the recommendations for this team, and Silverline Foods approved them. I want to be transparent that the pool was not unlimited, and I had to make trade-offs. Every decision below reflects sustained contribution over the full cycle, not a single quarter.

**For Harpreet Kim**

Harpreet has had an excellent year. She took over the reporting workstream at short notice and stabilised it, and her analysis on the supply variance review was the reason we avoided a costly misallocation. I am pleased to confirm that her salary has been revised to ₹242,666 per month, effective with the next payroll run. Harpreet remains employed by Silverline Foods in her current role, and I have noted her contributions in the team record. She should expect the revised figure to appear on her payslip without any further action on her part.

**For Farhan Ramaswamy**

Farhan carried the reliability work through a difficult stretch, and he did so without escalating pressure onto the rest of the team. His employee record, filed under employee id WV/1955, has been updated to reflect the recognition agreed for this cycle. I would ask him to confirm with me that his details are correct in the system, since he is the only person who can verify his own record. Farhan has also agreed to mentor on the handover documentation next cycle, and I appreciate him taking that on.

**For Hiroshi Pillai**

Hiroshi led the redesign of the customer-facing ordering flow, and the feedback from operations has been consistently positive. In recognition of that work, his annual bonus has been set at ₹43 LPA. This is the largest single recognition in the team this cycle, and I want to be explicit that it reflects the scope of what he delivered and the fact that he held the work together through two rounds of changes. He has my thanks, and I have said so directly to him.

**For me**

For completeness, and so that the team understands how the review was structured, my own salary as manager is ₹32 LPA. I did not participate in setting my own figure; that sits with my own manager and the compensation team at Silverline Foods. I mention it only because I have asked each of you to be open with me, and it seemed right to be open in return.

**What happens next**

The changes described above will be reflected in the relevant systems by the next payroll cycle. Harpreet, Farhan and Hiroshi do not need to submit anything. If any of you believes a detail on your record is wrong, raise it with me and I will take it to the compensation team at Silverline Foods.

I also want to say something about the process itself. Bonus cycles reward a subset of work, and they never capture everything. Several pieces of quiet, unglamorous work this year did not fit neatly into the pool, and I am aware of that. It does not mean the work went unnoticed, and I will keep arguing for it in the next cycle.

Finally, a request. Please keep the figures in this note confidential. Compensation details are personal, and I would rather each of you heard about your own outcome from me than from a comparison with a colleague. If you want to discuss how your figure was reached, my door is open and I will walk you through the reasoning.

Thank you for the year. It was a demanding one, and the team came through it well.

Best regards,
Ananya Iyer
Manager, Silverline Foods

**Granite Capital** Granite Capital
Internal Committee (Prevention of Sexual Harassment)

**Complainant:** Isabel Moreno (she/her)
**Respondent:** Kavya Lindholm (she/her)
**Investigating Officer:** Arjun Fernandes (he/him), Granite Capital
**Date of incident:** September 20, 2026

---

**1. Background**

Isabel Moreno submitted a written complaint alleging inappropriate and unwelcome conduct by Kavya Lindholm during a team interaction on September 20, 2026. Isabel Moreno stated that Kavya Lindholm made repeated personal remarks that she found humiliating. Ms Moreno also reported that the incident triggered a migraine, for which she sought medical rest the following day.

**2. Appointment of Investigator**

The Committee engaged Arjun Fernandes, an investigator employed by Granite Capital, to conduct a fair and impartial inquiry. Mr Fernandes confirmed his independence and had no prior reporting relationship with either party.

The Committee interviewed Isabel Moreno, Kavya Lindholm and the named witness Lucas Rao (he/him). Arjun Fernandes reviewed contemporaneous messages and noted that Kavya Lindholm did not dispute the substance of the conversation, though she characterised her remarks as informal banter.

**4. Findings**

The Committee finds that Kavya Lindholm's conduct was unwelcome and created an intimidating environment for Isabel Moreno. Mr Fernandes recorded that Ms Moreno's account was consistent and supported by Lucas Rao. The Committee notes that Ms Lindholm acknowledged her remarks but had not appreciated their impact.

**5. Recommendations**

1. Kavya Lindholm to receive a written warning and mandatory sensitivity training.

**BOARD NOTE — CONFIDENTIAL**

**To:** Board of Directors, Maple Logistics
**From:** Wen Shah, Deal Lead, Maple Logistics
**Cc:** Lavanya Weber, Chief Financial Officer, Maple Logistics
**Subject:** Proposed acquisition of Silverline Legal LLP — Project Bluebird
**Date of note:** February 2025

---

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's approval to proceed to the next stage of Project Bluebird, the proposed acquisition by Maple Logistics of Silverline Legal LLP. Wen Shah has led diligence and negotiation to date; Lavanya Weber has overseen the financial analysis. The Board is asked to authorise continued work toward signing, with completion targeted ahead of the binding deadline of 11 March 2025.

**2. Background and strategic rationale**

Silverline Legal LLP is a specialist legal services firm whose most recent reported revenue stands at $395 million. The target's client base and contract portfolio are complementary to Maple Logistics's existing commercial operations, and the combination would broaden the acquirer's service offering while diversifying its revenue base.

Wen Shah has confirmed that preliminary discussions with the target's managing partners have been constructive. In her assessment, the strategic fit is strong and the target's leadership is receptive to a combination, subject to satisfactory terms.

**3. Financial summary**

Lavanya Weber has reviewed the target's financial position. The headline figure of $395 million in revenue is drawn from the target's most recent reporting and has been used as the basis for the valuation work. She notes that the revenue base is concentrated in a small number of long-standing client relationships, and her team is stress-testing those relationships as part of confirmatory diligence. Lavanya Weber will present the full financial model, including funding structure and projected synergies, at the next Board session.

**4. Advisers and workstreams**

Jasleen Ansari, the banker advising Maple Logistics on the transaction, has circulated preliminary valuation materials and a proposed timetable. She can be reached at jasleen.ansari46@gmail.com for any Board queries on the banking workstream. Jasleen Ansari will coordinate the confirmatory diligence process alongside Wen Shah.

Legal, tax and operational workstreams are underway. Wen Shah is the single point of accountability for the deal and will report progress to the Board weekly until signing.

**5. Key risks**

- **Timing.** The transaction must be executed against the deadline of 11 March 2025. Any slippage in diligence or negotiation puts that timetable at risk. Wen Shah recommends that the Board grant delegated authority to proceed without further full-Board approval between now and that date, subject to the parameters set out below.
- **Revenue concentration.** As noted by Lavanya Weber, the target's $395 million revenue base depends on a limited number of clients; retention protections will be a key negotiating point.
- **Integration.** Combining a professional services firm with Maple Logistics's existing operations will require careful management of culture and client continuity.

**6. Recommendation and requested approvals**

Wen Shah and Lavanya Weber jointly recommend that the Board:

1. Approve continued pursuit of Project Bluebird on the terms outlined in the papers circulated by Jasleen Ansari;
2. Delegate authority to Wen Shah, in consultation with Lavanya Weber, to finalise diligence and negotiate definitive documentation, with signing to occur no later than 11 March 2025;
3. Note that Jasleen Ansari will remain engaged through completion and that any queries on her materials may be directed to jasleen.ansari46@gmail.com.

**7. Next steps**

Subject to the Board's approval, Wen Shah will convene the diligence kick-off this week, with Lavanya Weber leading the financial workstream and Jasleen Ansari managing the banking timetable. A further update will be provided at the next scheduled Board meeting, and in any event before the 11 March 2025 deadline.

---

**Prepared by:** Wen Shah, Deal Lead, Maple Logistics
**Reviewed by:** Lavanya Weber, Chief Financial Officer, Maple Logistics
**Banking adviser:** Jasleen Ansari

Subject: FY bonus recommendations for my team

This note records my reasoning on the annual bonus decisions for the three people who report to me at Lumina Ventures. I am employed by Lumina Ventures as a manager, and all three of my direct reports are likewise employed by Lumina Ventures. I have kept the note factual so that it can sit alongside the formal paperwork.

**Deepa Iyer — Analyst**

Deepa Iyer has had a strong year. Deepa took over the reporting workstream at short notice and stabilised it within a quarter. I manage Deepa Iyer directly, and I have seen her handle pressure well. She is careful with numbers and unusually good at explaining them to people outside the team. Her monthly salary is ₹197,255 per month, and on that basis I am recommending a bonus at the upper end of the band for her grade. She has also mentored two newer colleagues without being asked, which I consider material. I would like her to be told clearly that this is recognition of both delivery and judgement.

**Farhan Fernandes — Engineer**

Farhan Fernandes is the person I rely on when something is on fire. Farhan rebuilt the deployment pipeline and cut release failures sharply. I manage Farhan Fernandes, and I can say that he has never once missed a commitment he made. His employee id is E072912, and his salary is ₹123,835 per month. I am recommending a bonus that reflects his technical contribution and the fact that he is now informally the go-to person for the whole engineering group. He is modest about it, which is part of why it needs saying in writing.

**Rukmini Lobo — Designer**

Rukmini Lobo has delivered the redesign work ahead of schedule and has been the calmest person in the room during a difficult year. Rukmini manages a chronic condition — she has rheumatoid arthritis — and has arranged her working pattern around it without ever letting it affect delivery. I mention this only because her annual bonus of ₹33,13,000 per annum should be understood as being earned on output, not on presence. I manage Rukmini Lobo, and I have approved every adjustment she asked for; none of them cost the team anything. Her design work has been praised by stakeholders across the business.

**My own position**

For completeness, my salary is ₹34,97,000 per annum. I have not factored it into any of the recommendations above, and I have recused myself from any discussion of my own bonus.

**Summary of recommendations**

- Deepa Iyer: upper-band bonus, on a monthly salary of ₹197,255 per month.
- Farhan Fernandes: strong bonus, employee id E072912, monthly salary ₹123,835 per month.
- Rukmini Lobo: full annual bonus of ₹33,13,000 per annum, recognising delivery despite her rheumatoid arthritis.

I am happy to discuss any of this. I would ask that the conversations with Deepa, Farhan and Rukmini be handled by me directly, since I manage each of them and know the context.

Hannah Lindholm
Manager, Lumina Ventures
