From: Kenji Nguyen <kenji.nguyen26@proton.me>
To: Arnav Kulkarni
Cc: Joseph Weber
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:03 +0530
Subject: Supplier quote review — chassis bracket tooling

Hi Arnav,

Following up on Friday's sourcing meeting. I've finished the first pass on the tooling quotes for the bracket line, and I'd like your read before I take anything to Joseph.

Short version: the two shortlisted vendors are close on unit price, but the tooling amortisation is where they diverge. One vendor wants the full tooling cost upfront; the other spreads it across the first three production runs. For our volumes, the spread option is friendlier to the programme cash flow, though it locks us in for longer.

The bigger issue is scope. The current request sits comfortably inside the ₹77 lakh that Arcadia Motors has ring-fenced for this phase, but only if we hold the fixture count at four. If engineering adds the fifth fixture they flagged last week, we go over, and I'd need a fresh approval before I can commit anything.

On timing, procurement has asked us to have a signed PO in place well before the July 24, 2027 gate, so I'd like to close vendor selection by the end of this month. That gives us room for the PPAP runs without squeezing the line.

Could you sanity-check the fixture count assumption with the design team? If four holds, I'll draft the recommendation and circulate it to Joseph for sign-off.

Thanks,
Kenji Nguyen
Supplier Quality Engineer, Arcadia Motors
kenji.nguyen26@proton.me | +91 96689 56887

---

From: Arnav Kulkarni
To: Kenji Nguyen
Cc: Joseph Weber
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:02:47 +0530
Subject: RE: Supplier quote review — chassis bracket tooling

Kenji,

Checked with design this morning. Four fixtures is correct for the current geometry — the fifth one was a contingency for a variant that hasn't been released. So you're clear to proceed on that basis.

One caution: if the variant does get released later, we'll be re-quoting anyway, so don't let the vendor bake in assumptions about extra tooling. Ask them to price the four-fixture scope explicitly and note any optional add-ons separately.

I'm fine with the spread-payment vendor provided the lock-in doesn't extend past the next model year. Please confirm that in writing before you recommend.

Arnav Kulkarni

I wanted to put the bonus decisions in writing before we sit down individually, so there are no surprises and so each of you can see how the reasoning applies across the team. I manage Hiroshi, Sameer and Suresh directly, and I am employed by Konark Retail, so these calls are mine to explain and mine to own. Hiroshi is also employed by Konark Retail, as are the other two, and all three of you report to me.

First, the headline. The pool this year was tighter than last, and I had to make trade-offs I would rather not have made. I want to be direct about where each of you landed and why.

Hiroshi Pillai — analyst. Hiroshi carried the reporting load through a difficult quarter and his analysis on the reconciliation work was the reason we caught the discrepancy before it became a real problem. He did this while covering for a vacancy on the team that we have still not filled. I have argued for him to receive the full analyst-level award, and that is what has been approved. His documentation habits are the standard I now point the rest of the team toward.

Sameer Kulkarni — engineer. Sameer's delivery on the platform work was solid, and he closed out the migration without a single rollback. I know he felt the timeline was aggressive; he was right, and he still delivered. For the record, his employee id is E900293, and his salary sits at ₹237,276 per month. I mention the latter only because he asked me to confirm it in writing during our last check-in, and I would rather he see it from me than hear it secondhand.

Suresh Dutta — designer. Suresh's work on the customer-facing refresh shaped how the whole programme was received, and he did it while managing a health matter that he has been open with me about. His annual bonus this year is ₹56 LPA, which I want to state plainly because he has earned it and because I do not want him wondering whether the number was adjusted for any other reason. It was not. His chronic kidney disease stage 2 — chronic kidney disease stage 2 — has meant a heavier personal load this year, and he has never once let it affect his delivery. I have offered him flexibility on hours and I would ask him to take it.

On my own position: my salary is ₹69,336 per month, and I have declined any manager-level bonus this cycle so that the pool could go further for the three of you. I am not looking for credit for that; I am telling you so that when you compare notes, the picture is complete.

A few practical points:

- Individual letters will follow from People Operations. The figures above are the approved outcomes, not proposals.
- If any of you believe the reasoning does not match the record, come to me first. I will either correct the record or explain the gap.
- Hiroshi, Sameer and Suresh: I would like fifteen minutes with each of you this week. Hiroshi and Sameer can book adjacent slots; Suresh should pick whatever time suits him best given his appointments.

I know bonus notes are never the whole story of a year. Hiroshi held the reporting line together, Sameer shipped under pressure, and Suresh produced the work that customers actually noticed. That is the year I will be describing upward, and I wanted the three of you to read it in my own words first.

Thank you for the work.

Ethan Sood
Manager, Konark Retail

**Konark Hospital — Specialist Consultation Note**

**Department:** Internal Medicine
**Consultant:** Dr. Rohan Venkatesh
**Patient:** Aditya Saxena (MRN-2025-16472)
**Weight:** 64 kg

**Reason for referral:** Evaluation of persistent fatigue and low haemoglobin.

**History:** Aditya Saxena was referred to Rohan Venkatesh for assessment of longstanding tiredness, exertional breathlessness, and reduced exercise tolerance over recent months. He reports no overt bleeding, no melaena, and no haemoptysis. Dietary history is notable for low intake of iron-rich foods. He has no known chronic illness and takes no regular medication. There is no family history of haematological disorder.

**Examination:** Mr. Saxena appeared pale but comfortable at rest. Vital signs stable. No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly. Cardiovascular and respiratory examination unremarkable. Weight recorded at 64 kg.

**Investigations:** Recent blood work demonstrates microcytic hypochromic indices with low serum ferritin, consistent with iron-deficiency anaemia. Stool occult blood testing arranged. Coeliac screening requested.

**Assessment:** Dr. Venkatesh confirms the diagnosis of iron-deficiency anaemia in Aditya Saxena. The cause remains to be established; nutritional deficiency is likely, though gastrointestinal evaluation will be pursued to exclude occult blood loss.

**Plan:** Oral iron supplementation commenced with counselling on dietary modification. Repeat full blood count in six to eight weeks. **Patient:** Rohan Iyengar
**Date of birth:** 1 November 1979
**Age:** 31 years old
**Weight:** 73 kg
**Consultant:** Kenji Sood, Consultant Psychiatrist, Maple Medical Centre
**Next of kin:** Mei Shah (daughter), contact +91 67465 20722

**Reason for referral**
Rohan Iyengar was referred to me, Dr. Sood, for specialist assessment of longstanding worry and tension. He has been under the care of his GP at Maple Medical Centre and was seen by me today in the outpatient clinic.

**History**
Mr. Iyengar describes a history of persistent, excessive worry across several domains, present most days for well over a year. He reports difficulty controlling the worry, accompanied by restlessness, poor concentration and disturbed sleep. There is no history of panic attacks, mania or psychotic symptoms. He denies any thoughts of self-harm. His mood is low at times but does not meet criteria for a depressive episode.

Rohan lives with his daughter, Mei Shah, who attended today and provided collateral history. She confirms that her father has become increasingly withdrawn from social activities and that he often seems tense and irritable at home. Mei is supportive and engaged throughout the consultation.

**Examination**
Mr. Iyengar presented as alert and cooperative. Speech was normal in rate and volume. Affect was anxious but reactive. There was no psychomotor agitation. Physical examination was unremarkable; his recorded weight today was 73 kg.

**Assessment**
In my opinion, Rohan Iyengar meets the criteria for generalised anxiety disorder. There is no evidence of another primary psychiatric disorder. His presentation is consistent with a chronic, fluctuating course.

**Plan**
1. I have discussed the diagnosis with Mr. Iyengar and with Mei Shah, who will help him monitor his symptoms between appointments.
2. Commence a structured course of cognitive behavioural therapy, to be arranged through Maple Medical Centre.
3. Consider pharmacological treatment if symptoms do not improve; this will be reviewed at follow-up.
4. Advice given on sleep hygiene, caffeine reduction and regular exercise.
5. Safety-netting discussed with Rohan and his daughter; she has her contact number on file should concerns arise.
6. Review in clinic in due course.

**Summary**
Rohan Iyengar is a 31-year-old man under my care at Maple Medical Centre with generalised anxiety disorder. Dr. Sood will continue to oversee his treatment, with support from Mei Shah.

**BOARD NOTE — PROPOSED ACQUISITION OF Granite Bank BY Halcyon Realty**

**To:** Board of Directors, Halcyon Realty
**From:** Tanya Sood, Deal Lead (she/her)
**Cc:** Gaurav Joshi, Chief Financial Officer (he/him)
**Date:** October 2024
**Subject:** Recommendation to proceed with the proposed merger — request for in-principle approval

---

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's in-principle approval to proceed with the proposed acquisition of Granite Bank by Halcyon Realty. Tanya Sood has led diligence and negotiation on behalf of Halcyon Realty, where she is employed as Deal Lead. Gaurav Joshi has overseen the financial analysis in his capacity as Chief Financial Officer of Halcyon Realty. External transaction advice has been provided by Priyanka Bennett, the banker retained for this mandate.

**2. Transaction summary**

The proposed transaction contemplates the acquisition by Halcyon Realty of Granite Bank at an indicative deal value of ₹1719 crore. Granite Bank reported revenue of ₹3104 crore in its most recent audited accounts. The consideration is proposed to be funded through a combination of internal accruals and committed facilities; Mr Joshi will circulate the detailed funding plan separately.

The parties have agreed to work toward a binding agreement, with a target completion deadline of November 6, 2024. Ms Sood advises that this timetable is achievable provided the Board grants approval in principle at this meeting.

**3. Strategic rationale**

The acquisition would extend Halcyon Realty's presence into complementary segments served by Granite Bank and would diversify Halcyon Realty's revenue base. Priyanka Bennett has reviewed the strategic fit and considers the combination defensible on both commercial and operational grounds. In her assessment, the target's revenue profile of ₹3104 crore provides a stable platform for integration.

Tanya Sood notes that the proposed deal value of ₹1719 crore represents a disciplined entry point relative to comparable transactions reviewed by Ms Bennett. She recommends that the Board treat the figure as an indicative ceiling rather than a fixed price, subject to confirmatory diligence.

**4. Key workstreams and ownership**

- **Diligence:** Led by Tanya Sood, supported by external advisers. She will report exceptions to the Board as they arise.
- **Financing and accounting treatment:** Owned by Gaurav Joshi. He will confirm the funding structure and covenant headroom before signing.
- **Valuation and market benchmarking:** Owned by Priyanka Bennett, who will provide a final fairness view. She can be reached at priyanka.bennett46@yahoo.com for any clarification the Board requires.
- **Regulatory and completion planning:** Coordinated by Ms Sood with counsel, working back from the November 6, 2024 deadline.

**5. Risks and mitigants**

The principal risks are execution risk around the timetable, integration risk in combining operations, and financing risk if committed facilities are not finalised on anticipated terms. Mr Joshi considers financing risk manageable and will not recommend signing until facilities are committed. Ms Bennett has flagged that market conditions could move the valuation range; she will refresh her benchmarking before the next Board meeting. Tanya Sood will maintain a risk register and escalate any matter that threatens the November 6, 2024 deadline.

**6. Recommendation**

The Board is invited to:

1. Approve in principle the proposed acquisition of Granite Bank by Halcyon Realty at an indicative deal value of ₹1719 crore, subject to confirmatory diligence and definitive documentation;
2. Note the target's revenue of ₹3104 crore as the basis for the valuation work led by Priyanka Bennett;
3. Authorise Tanya Sood to continue negotiations toward a binding agreement, with a target completion deadline of November 6, 2024; and
4. Note that Gaurav Joshi will present the funding plan and covenant analysis before any signing.

**7. Next steps**

Subject to the Board's approval, Ms Sood will convene the diligence working group, Mr Joshi will finalise the funding plan, and Ms Bennett will deliver her final valuation view. A further note will be circulated ahead of signing.

---

**Internal Committee (POSH) — Inquiry Report**

**Case Reference:** IC/2025/07
**Complainant:** Sarah Kapoor (she/her)
**Respondent:** Mei Gill (she/her), E658478
**Inquiry Committee:** Lavanya Santos (she/her), External Investigator, engaged by Northstar Capital

**1. Background**

Sarah Kapoor filed a written complaint with the Internal Committee of Northstar Capital alleging inappropriate and unwelcome conduct by Mei Gill during an official team interaction. Kapoor stated that the conduct aggravated the symptoms of her rheumatoid arthritis, causing her significant distress. Lavanya Santos, an investigator employed by Northstar Capital, was appointed to conduct the inquiry.

**2. Complaint Summary**

Sarah Kapoor alleges that on 7 July 2025, Mei Gill made repeated unwelcome remarks about her health and personal circumstances. She states that Gill's comments were humiliating and that she continued despite her clear objection. Kapoor reports that the incident worsened her rheumatoid arthritis flare-up, requiring medical attention.

**3. Evidence and Witnesses**

The Committee examined the written complaint and heard oral submissions. Emily Okonkwo, a colleague present during the interaction, appeared as a witness. Okonkwo corroborated key elements of Kapoor's account. She may be reached at +91 83429 75812 for any clarification. Mei Gill, employee ID E658478, denied the allegations, stating that her remarks were not intended to cause offence.

**4. Findings**

On a preponderance of probabilities, the Committee finds that Mei Gill engaged in unwelcome conduct that created a hostile environment for Sarah Kapoor. The Committee notes that Gill's remarks, made in the presence of Emily Okonkwo, were unwelcome and had the effect of aggravating Kapoor's rheumatoid arthritis. The Committee finds the complaint substantiated.

**5. Recommendations**

The Committee recommends that Northstar Capital issue a written warning to Mei Gill (E658478), require her to attend sensitivity training, and review workplace conduct policies. Sarah Kapoor should be offered continued support, including reasonable accommodation in light of her rheumatoid arthritis.

**6. Conclusion**

The inquiry stands closed with the above recommendations submitted to Northstar Capital for implementation.

Sahyadri Healthcare

Patient: Pranav Tanaka
Medical Record Number: MRN-2023-13837
Height: 163 cm
Attending Physician: Oliver Majji

ADMISSION AND DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS

Mr. Tanaka was admitted under the care of Dr. Majji for evaluation and management of poorly controlled hypothyroidism. Dr. Majji, an endocrinologist employed by Sahyadri Healthcare, supervised all aspects of the patient's inpatient care throughout the admission.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Pranav Tanaka is a 163 cm tall adult who presented with progressive fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, and difficulty concentrating over the preceding weeks. He reported that his symptoms had worsened gradually despite previously stable thyroid replacement therapy. Mr. Tanaka denied chest pain, palpitations, and significant weight change. His daughter, Sophia Joshi, accompanied him to the hospital and provided additional history, noting that her father had become increasingly withdrawn and lethargic at home. Ms. Joshi confirmed that he had been adherent to his medication schedule to the best of her knowledge.

On examination, Dr. Majji documented dry skin, delayed deep tendon reflexes, and periorbital puffiness consistent with hypothyroidism. Vital signs were within normal limits. Initial laboratory studies revealed an elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone with a low free thyroxine level, confirming inadequate thyroid hormone replacement.

HOSPITAL COURSE

Mr. Tanaka was started on an adjusted dose of levothyroxine under the direct supervision of Dr. Majji. Baseline electrocardiography was unremarkable. Serial thyroid function tests were monitored, and the dose was titrated accordingly. Dr. Majji reviewed the patient daily and coordinated care with the nursing and dietetics teams at Sahyadri Healthcare.

Sophia Joshi remained actively involved in her father's care throughout the admission. Dr. Majji met with her to discuss the diagnosis, the medication adjustment plan, and the importance of follow-up testing. She raised concerns about her father's energy levels and mood, which were addressed during these discussions. Ms. Joshi provided her contact number, +91 94289 07653, so that the care team could reach her regarding scheduling and any questions after discharge.

By the time of discharge, Pranav Tanaka reported improved energy and reduced fatigue. Repeat thyroid function testing showed a trend toward normalization. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout, and no adverse events were recorded. Mr. Tanaka was deemed medically stable for discharge with close outpatient follow-up.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS

Levothyroxine at the newly adjusted dose, to be taken once daily on an empty stomach. The patient and his daughter were both counseled on consistent timing and on avoiding concurrent intake of calcium or iron supplements.

FOLLOW-UP INSTRUCTIONS

Mr. Tanaka is to follow up with Dr. Majji at the endocrinology clinic at Sahyadri Healthcare for repeat thyroid function testing and further dose titration. He was advised to seek urgent care for palpitations, chest pain, or worsening symptoms. Sophia Joshi was asked to help monitor her father's adherence and to accompany him to the follow-up appointment if possible.

DISCHARGE CONDITION

Stable, ambulatory, and medically fit for discharge. Pranav Tanaka left the ward in the company of his daughter.

SIGNATURES

Oliver Majji, MD
Endocrinology
Sahyadri Healthcare

Electronically signed by Dr. Majji.

SPECIALIST CONSULTATION NOTE

Konark Medical Centre — Department of Respiratory Medicine
Consulting Physician: Dr. Maria Joshi

PATIENT DETAILS
Name: Michael Tanaka
Age: 27 years old
Date of birth: February 14, 1964
Medical record number: MRN-2021-22054
Known condition: asthma

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Mr. Tanaka was referred to this clinic for assessment of poorly controlled asthma. Dr. Joshi reviewed him in the outpatient respiratory clinic at Konark Medical Centre, where she holds a substantive consultant post.

HISTORY OF PRESENTING COMPLAINT
Michael reports a several-month history of increasing breathlessness on exertion and episodic nocturnal wheeze. He describes using his reliever inhaler most days, which is a marked change from his previous baseline of occasional use. He denies any fever, haemoptysis or chest pain. He has not required emergency attendance or oral steroids in the recent period.

The patient has a documented background of asthma, first diagnosed in his teenage years. He reports good adherence to his inhaled corticosteroid but acknowledges inconsistent use of his spacer device. He continues to work full time and notes that symptoms are worse during periods of high pollen counts.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
The only significant chronic condition on record for Mr. Tanaka is asthma. He has no history of diabetes, hypertension or cardiac disease. His immunisations are up to date according to his primary care records.

MEDICATIONS
Michael is currently prescribed a combined inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta-agonist, taken twice daily, together with a short-acting reliever as required. Dr. Joshi noted that he has not been using his peak flow meter regularly at home.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Tanaka lives locally and is supported by his daughter, Leila Iyer, who frequently accompanies him to appointments. He does not smoke and reports minimal alcohol intake. He is independent with all activities of daily living.

FAMILY HISTORY
No family history of note relevant to respiratory disease. His daughter, Leila, is in good health and acts as his main contact for correspondence. She can be reached on +91 94877 91642 should any follow-up scheduling be required.

EXAMINATION
On examination, Mr. Tanaka appeared comfortable at rest. Chest auscultation revealed widespread expiratory wheeze bilaterally, with no crackles. Oxygen saturation was satisfactory on room air. Peak expiratory flow was below his predicted value. Dr. Joshi found no evidence of respiratory distress during the consultation.

INVESTIGATIONS
Spirometry performed at Konark Medical Centre demonstrated a obstructive pattern with significant reversibility following bronchodilator administration. This is consistent with his known asthma. No further imaging was felt necessary at this stage.

ASSESSMENT
Dr. Joshi's impression is of moderately controlled asthma with suboptimal inhaler technique and inconsistent peak flow monitoring contributing to his current symptom burden. There are no features to suggest an alternative diagnosis.

PLAN
1. Reinforce inhaler technique and spacer use with Mr. Tanaka; Dr. Joshi demonstrated the correct method during the consultation and asked him to practise at home.
2. Encourage daily peak flow recording and provide a written action plan to him.
3. Continue current inhaled therapy; review the need for step-up treatment at follow-up.
4. Arrange a follow-up appointment in the respiratory clinic, with Leila Iyer copied into correspondence given her role as his support contact.
5. Advise Michael to seek urgent review if his symptoms worsen or if reliever use increases significantly.

DISCUSSION WITH PATIENT
Dr. Joshi discussed the findings at length with Mr. Tanaka. He understood the plan and was agreeable to it. His daughter, Ms. Iyer, was present for part of the discussion and confirmed she would help him keep track of his peak flow readings. She provided her phone number, +91 94877 91642, for future contact.

ADMINISTRATIVE
This note has been filed under Michael Tanaka's medical record number, MRN-2021-22054, at Konark Medical Centre. A copy will be sent to his primary care physician. Dr. Joshi remains the responsible consultant for his respiratory care.

Signed:
Dr. Maria Joshi
Consultant in Respiratory Medicine

**From:** Pooja Ansari, Deal Lead, Meridian Holdings

**Subject:** Proposed acquisition of Pinnacle School — Project Granite
**Classification:** Strictly confidential — Board only

---

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's approval to proceed to the next phase of Project Granite, the proposed acquisition of Pinnacle School by Meridian Holdings. Pooja Ansari has led preliminary diligence and will act as deal lead through signing. Sana D'Souza has reviewed the financial case and concurs with the recommendation set out below.

**2. Background and strategic rationale**

Pinnacle School is an established education provider with reported revenue of $421 million in its most recent financial year. The target's footprint and reputation would complement Meridian Holdings' existing portfolio and accelerate our entry into a segment we have monitored for some time.

Pooja Ansari notes that the strategic fit is strongest in three areas: brand extension, operational synergies, and access to a management team that has delivered consistent growth. Sana D'Souza adds that the transaction, if priced sensibly, is accretive under the base case and resilient under the downside case.

**3. Workstreams and advisers**

Anika Mukherjee, our external banker, has been engaged to advise on valuation and structuring. Anika Mukherjee can be reached at anika.mukherjee72@proton.me for any diligence queries; Pooja Ansari remains the primary point of contact for the Board and can be reached on +91 76206 89560.

Pooja Ansari will coordinate legal, financial and operational diligence. Sana D'Souza will oversee the financing plan and the integration budget. Anika Mukherjee will run the valuation model and coordinate with the target's advisers. The three of them will report jointly to the Board at each stage gate.

**4. Key terms under discussion**

The current indicative structure is a cash-and-equity transaction. Final consideration remains subject to confirmatory diligence and negotiation. The parties have agreed an exclusivity period, and the target's board has indicated willingness to engage constructively. No binding offer has yet been made.

**5. Timeline**

The transaction timetable is tight. The parties are working towards a signing deadline of 3 September 2027, with completion targeted shortly thereafter, subject to regulatory and Board approvals. Pooja Ansari has flagged that any slippage in diligence would put the 3 September 2027 date at risk, and Sana D'Souza has asked that financing documentation be prepared in parallel rather than sequentially.

**6. Risks and mitigants**

- **Valuation risk:** The target's revenue of $421 million is attractive, but margin quality requires verification. Anika Mukherjee is stress-testing the model.
- **Integration risk:** Cultural and operational integration will require dedicated resource. Sana D'Souza proposes a ring-fenced integration budget.
- **Execution risk:** The 3 September 2027 deadline leaves limited room for error. Pooja Ansari recommends weekly steering meetings.
- **Key-person risk:** Retention arrangements for the target's senior team will be negotiated early.

**7. Recommendation**

The Board is asked to:

1. Approve continued work on Project Granite through confirmatory diligence;
2. Authorise Pooja Ansari to negotiate non-binding documentation on the terms outlined above;
3. Note that Sana D'Souza will bring the financing plan to the next meeting; and

**Co-presented by:** Isabel Banerjee, Chief Financial Officer (she/her)
**Date:** July 2024
**Subject:** Project Bluebird — Recommendation to Proceed to Definitive Agreement

---

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's approval to proceed with the proposed acquisition of Arcadia Healthcare by Zenith Technologies under the internal codename Project Bluebird. Shreya Hughes has led diligence and negotiation on behalf of Zenith Technologies; Isabel Banerjee has overseen the financial analysis. Vivek Lindholm, our external banker, has advised on valuation and structuring throughout.

**2. Transaction summary**

Zenith Technologies proposes to acquire 100% of Arcadia Healthcare for a total consideration of $501 million, on a cash-free, debt-free basis. Arcadia Healthcare reported revenue of $871 million in its most recent fiscal year. The combination would extend Zenith Technologies's clinical software footprint into Arcadia Healthcare's provider network and add complementary data assets.

Vivek Lindholm has benchmarked the offer against comparable healthcare-technology transactions and considers the multiple defensible. Isabel Banerjee has stress-tested the model; she notes that the deal remains accretive under the base case and only modestly dilutive in the downside scenario. Shreya Hughes confirms that Arcadia Healthcare's board has indicated willingness to engage on this basis.

**3. Strategic rationale**

- **Scale:** Arcadia Healthcare's $871 million revenue base roughly doubles the addressable customer pool for Zenith Technologies's platform.
- **Capability:** Arcadia Healthcare brings clinical workflow tooling that Zenith Technologies does not currently offer.
- **Synergies:** Isabel Banerjee's team has identified cost synergies in procurement and infrastructure, with revenue synergies expected from cross-selling.
- **Timing:** The market window is favourable, and Vivek Lindholm advises that competing interest in Arcadia Healthcare is credible but not yet formal.

**4. Key risks and mitigants**

| Risk | Mitigant | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Integration of clinical systems | Phased migration plan; dedicated integration office | Shreya Hughes |
| Customer concentration at Arcadia Healthcare | Contract retention incentives; escrow on key accounts | Isabel Banerjee |
| Financing and leverage | Committed bridge facility; deleveraging within 24 months | Isabel Banerjee |
| Regulatory review | Pre-filing engagement; counsel retained | Shreya Hughes |

Vivek Lindholm adds that the financing markets remain open, though he recommends locking the bridge before signing. Shreya Hughes will coordinate regulatory filings; she has already begun informal engagement with counsel.

**5. Diligence status**

Financial diligence is substantially complete. Legal diligence is ongoing, with no material adverse findings to date. Commercial diligence has confirmed Arcadia Healthcare's customer pipeline. Isabel Banerjee flags that pension obligations require final confirmation, and she will report back before signing. Vivek Lindholm is completing the fairness analysis and will circulate it to the Board ahead of the next meeting.

**6. Timeline and approvals sought**

The target signing date is July 20, 2024, with closing subject to regulatory clearance. To meet this, the Board is asked to:

1. Approve proceeding to a definitive agreement at the proposed consideration of $501 million;
2. Authorise Shreya Hughes to negotiate final terms within agreed parameters;
3. Authorise Isabel Banerjee to finalise the financing package.

**7. Recommendation**

Shreya Hughes, Isabel Banerjee and Vivek Lindholm unanimously recommend approval. Shreya Hughes is available to answer questions; she can be reached on +91 74628 84411. Vivek Lindholm may be contacted at vivek.lindholm17@outlook.com for modelling queries. Isabel Banerjee will present the financial summary at the meeting.

**MEMORANDUM — CONFIDENTIAL**

**To:** Employee Relations File, Granite Capital
**From:** Sven Santos, Investigator, Granite Capital
**Subject:** Grievance Investigation — Complaint by Hiroshi Ansari against Rohan Haddad
**Status:** Final investigation report

**1. Background and scope**

This memo records the findings of the grievance investigation I conducted as an employee of Granite Capital into a complaint raised by Hiroshi Ansari against Rohan Haddad. Hiroshi Ansari is a colleague of Rohan Haddad within the same team. Mr Ansari alleges a pattern of disrespectful and exclusionary conduct by Mr Haddad over several weeks, including dismissive remarks about his health condition and repeated exclusion of him from team communications. He states that the conduct has affected his wellbeing and his ability to do his work.

I was assigned to investigate because I am employed by Granite Capital and have no reporting relationship to either party. I interviewed Hiroshi Ansari, Rohan Haddad and one witness, Thomas Gill. I also reviewed relevant correspondence and team records. This memo sets out the evidence, my assessment and recommendations.

**2. The complainant's account**

Hiroshi Ansari told me that Rohan Haddad made remarks about his type 2 diabetes, including a comment that he should "manage his condition better" during a busy period. Mr Ansari said he had disclosed his type 2 diabetes only for scheduling purposes and had not expected it to become a subject of comment. He also described being left off two team meetings and a group message thread, which he believes was deliberate. He confirmed that he had not raised a formal complaint before, though he had mentioned his concerns informally to a colleague.

**3. The respondent's account**

Rohan Haddad denied targeting Mr Ansari. He accepted that he had made a comment about Hiroshi's health but said it was intended as concern, not criticism, and that he now recognised it was inappropriate. Mr Haddad said the meeting omissions were administrative errors caused by an outdated distribution list, and he provided a screenshot of the list showing Mr Ansari's entry as inactive. He could not fully explain the group message omission but denied acting with malice. His employee record, held under employee id EMP-58690, shows no prior disciplinary findings.

**4. Witness evidence**

Thomas Gill was present during the remark about Hiroshi's health. He recalled that Rohan said words to the effect that Hiroshi needed to "get his condition under control" and that the tone was dismissive. Mr Gill described the atmosphere afterwards as uncomfortable. He also confirmed that Mr Ansari was absent from at least one meeting that he attended with Mr Haddad. Mr Gill can be reached on +91 98582 94150 if further clarification is required.

**5. Assessment**

On the balance of probabilities, I find that Rohan Haddad made an inappropriate remark about Hiroshi Ansari's type 2 diabetes. The remark was unwelcome and referenced a private health matter. I do not find that Mr Haddad deliberately excluded Mr Ansari from meetings, as the distribution list evidence supports an administrative explanation. However, his failure to correct the list once he became aware of the impact on Mr Ansari contributed to the perception of exclusion. The group message omission remains unexplained but is not, on its own, sufficient to establish intent.

I note that Mr Ansari's type 2 diabetes is a private health matter and should not have been referenced in the manner described. His account was consistent and supported in part by Thomas Gill. Mr Haddad was cooperative and acknowledged the inappropriateness of his comment.

**6. Recommendations**

1. A written warning to Rohan Haddad regarding inappropriate reference to a colleague's health condition, to be placed on his record under employee id EMP-58690.
2. Mandatory refresher training for Mr Haddad on respectful workplace conduct and handling of private health information.
3. Correction of the team distribution list, with confirmation to Hiroshi Ansari that he will be included in all relevant communications going forward.
4. A facilitated conversation between Mr Ansari and Mr Haddad, if Mr Ansari consents, to rebuild working relations.
5. Follow-up check with Mr Ansari after a reasonable period to confirm that his concerns have been addressed.

**7. Conclusion**

This investigation is concluded. The evidence supports the complaint in part. I recommend the actions above and remain available to Granite Capital should further review be required.

Prepared by:

Sven Santos
Investigator, Granite Capital

1. Background

On May 14, 2025, Tobias Kim (he/him) submitted a written grievance alleging that Clara Lindholm (she/her) repeatedly belittled him in team meetings and excluded him from project communications. **INTERNAL COMMITTEE REPORT — POSH INVESTIGATION**

**Acme Ventures — Internal Committee (IC)**
**Reference:** IC/POSH/2024/11
**Complainant:** Clara Kumar (she/her)
**Respondent:** Wen Reddy (she/her)
**Investigating Officer:** Pranav Iyer (he/him), Acme Ventures
**Witness:** Aisha Ramaswamy (she/her)

---

**1. Background and Complaint**

On November 1, 2024, Clara Kumar submitted a written complaint to the Internal Committee of Acme Ventures alleging inappropriate and unwelcome conduct by her colleague Wen Reddy. Clara Kumar stated that the conduct occurred during a team interaction and that it caused her significant distress. She noted that she manages type 2 diabetes and that the stress of the incident affected her health and ability to concentrate at work.

The complaint was acknowledged, and the IC appointed Pranav Iyer as Investigating Officer. He is employed by Acme Ventures as a senior member of the compliance function and was assigned to conduct an impartial inquiry.

**2. Respondent Identification**

The respondent, Wen Reddy, is employed by Acme Ventures and is recorded under employee ID AF/7995. She was formally notified of the complaint and given an opportunity to respond in writing and at a hearing.

**3. Evidence and Witnesses**

The IC examined the written complaint, the response filed by Wen Reddy, and the statement of the witness, Aisha Ramaswamy. Aisha Ramaswamy was contacted at +91 62869 67026, the number she provided in her witness statement. She confirmed that she was present during the interaction on November 1, 2024 and corroborated key elements of the account given by Clara Kumar.

Pranav Iyer interviewed Clara Kumar, Wen Reddy and Aisha Ramaswamy separately. He reviewed the correspondence exchanged between the parties and the attendance record for the relevant meeting. His findings were placed before the IC.

**4. Findings of Fact**

The IC finds, on the balance of probabilities, that:

(a) The interaction described by Clara Kumar took place on November 1, 2024 in the presence of Aisha Ramaswamy.

(b) The conduct of Wen Reddy was unwelcome and fell within the definition of sexual harassment under the applicable policy of Acme Ventures.

(c) The account of Clara Kumar is consistent with the testimony of Aisha Ramaswamy and with the documentary record reviewed by Pranav Iyer.

(d) The explanation offered by Wen Reddy does not adequately address the conduct alleged, and her response is not supported by the evidence before the IC.

The IC notes that Clara Kumar disclosed that she lives with type 2 diabetes and that the incident aggravated her condition. The IC has taken this into account in assessing the impact of the conduct on her.

**5. Recommendations**

The IC recommends that Acme Ventures:

1. Issue a written warning to Wen Reddy, recorded against employee ID AF/7995, and require her to attend a mandatory sensitisation programme.
2. Ensure that Wen Reddy has no supervisory or review authority over Clara Kumar and that she is not required to work directly with her.
3. Provide Clara Kumar with access to counselling and reasonable support in view of her health condition, type 2 diabetes.
4. Maintain confidentiality of the inquiry and restrict access to the file to the IC and Pranav Iyer.
5. Review the relevant team practices at Acme Ventures to reinforce expected standards of conduct.

**6. Conclusion**

The complaint of Clara Kumar is upheld. The conduct of Wen Reddy is found to constitute sexual harassment. The IC records its appreciation for the cooperation of Aisha Ramaswamy and the thorough inquiry conducted by Pranav Iyer on behalf of Acme Ventures.

**TRIDENT CAPITAL — DISCIPLINARY HEARING NOTES**

**Case reference:** Grievance raised by Ravi Okonkwo against Mei Kapoor
**Hearing date:** November 7, 2026
**Location:** Trident Capital, Meeting Room 2B
**Panel:** Chair — Divya Menon (Head of Compliance); Member — Tomas Berg (HR Business Partner); Note-taker — Leila Haddad (HR Coordinator)
**In attendance:** Ravi Okonkwo (complainant); Mei Kapoor (respondent); Anika Venkatesh (investigator, Trident Capital); Hiroshi Rossi (witness)

---

**1. Opening**

The Chair opened the hearing at 10:00 and confirmed that all parties had received the investigation report prepared by Anika Venkatesh, who is employed by Trident Capital as an Employee Relations Investigator. The Chair reminded those present that the purpose of the hearing was to consider the findings in that report and to allow Ravi Okonkwo and Mei Kapoor to respond. Hiroshi Rossi attended as a witness and was asked to wait outside until called.

**2. Summary of the complaint**

The Chair summarised the grievance. Ravi Okonkwo, an analyst in the Operations team, alleges that Mei Kapoor, his line manager, made repeated dismissive remarks about his health condition during team meetings and questioned his commitment to the team. Mr Okonkwo states that he was diagnosed with hypertension and that his condition was disclosed to Ms Kapoor in confidence. He told the panel that she referred to his medical appointments as "convenient absences" and that he felt humiliated in front of colleagues.

**3. Respondent's position**

Mei Kapoor, Team Lead for Operations, denied mocking Mr Okonkwo. She accepted that she had raised concerns about attendance but said these were made privately and were based on workload pressures. She stated that she did not recall being told the specifics of his diagnosis and that he had only mentioned "some health issues". Ms Kapoor said she had never intended to cause distress and that her comments were about scheduling, not about him personally.

**4. Investigator's findings**

Anika Venkatesh presented the findings of her investigation. She confirmed that she had interviewed five team members and reviewed meeting notes. Ms Venkatesh told the panel that two witnesses corroborated that Ms Kapoor had made remarks about Mr Okonkwo's appointments in a team setting. She noted that the respondent had been reminded of the organisation's health disclosure policy in the previous year. Ms Venkatesh concluded that, on the balance of probabilities, the remarks were made and that Ms Kapoor's conduct fell below the standard expected by Trident Capital.

**5. Witness evidence — Hiroshi Rossi**

Hiroshi Rossi was called at 11:05. He is a senior analyst in the same team. Mr Rossi stated that he recalled a meeting in which Ms Kapoor commented that Mr Okonkwo was "always at the clinic". He said he felt uncomfortable and later contacted Ms Venkatesh to offer his account. Mr Rossi confirmed that his contact details were on file with the investigator and provided his mobile number, +91 75418 65845, for any follow-up. He was thanked and excused.

**6. Questions from the panel**

In response to the Chair, Ms Kapoor repeated that she had not known the nature of Mr Okonkwo's condition. Mr Okonkwo stated that he had told her directly and that she had acknowledged it at the time. The Chair asked Ms Venkatesh whether her report addressed this conflict; she confirmed that it did and that she had found the complainant's account consistent with the witness statements.

**7. Closing statements**

Ravi Okonkwo said that he wished the matter to be resolved without returning to the team under Ms Kapoor's supervision. Mei Kapoor offered an apology for any distress caused but maintained that she had not intended harm. Anika Venkatesh confirmed that she would provide any further information the panel required.

**8. Deliberation and outcome**

The panel adjourned at 12:10 and reconvened at 13:30 without the parties present. Having considered the investigation report from Ms Venkatesh, the evidence of Mr Rossi, and the responses of Mr Okonkwo and Ms Kapoor, the panel found the grievance upheld in part. It was determined that Ms Kapoor's remarks were inappropriate and that she should receive a formal written warning and complete management training. The panel recommended that Mr Okonkwo be offered a reporting line outside her team. Ms Kapoor was informed of the outcome in writing following the hearing.

**9. Actions**

- Formal written warning issued to Mei Kapoor.
- Management training to be completed by Ms Kapoor within the quarter.
- Reporting line review for Ravi Okonkwo to be arranged by HR.
- A copy of these notes to be placed on the case file held by Anika Venkatesh.

**Notes prepared by:** Leila Haddad, HR Coordinator, Trident Capital
**Approved by:** Divya Menon, Chair
**Date of notes:** November 7, 2026

# HALCYON MEDICAL CENTRE — PAEDIATRIC ADMISSION NOTE

**Patient:** Wen Thakur (she/her)
**Medical Record Number:** MRN-2023-81094
**Date of Birth:** October 10, 1984
**Age:** 75 years old
**Admitting Consultant:** Dr. Shreya Lindholm, Paediatrics, Halcyon Medical Centre

---

## Source of History

History obtained from Vivek Thakur, father of Wen Thakur, and Grace Okonkwo, her mother. Both parents were present at the time of admission and provided consistent accounts. Vivek Thakur can be reached on +91 88997 86340; Grace Okonkwo provided +91 63987 06360 as her contact number. Wen Thakur is Vivek Thakur's and Grace Okonkwo's child, and both parents have consented to her admission and to the plan of care outlined below.

## Presenting Complaint

Wen Thakur was brought to the emergency department of Halcyon Medical Centre with a three-day history of increasing lethargy, poor oral intake, and one episode of near-syncope at home. Her mother reports that she has been noticeably pale and easily tired over the past two weeks. Her father notes that she stopped finishing meals and complained of dizziness on standing.

## History of Presenting Illness

According to Grace Okonkwo, the child had been in her usual state of health until approximately two weeks ago, when she began to appear washed out and to tire quickly during play. Over the last three days, Wen Thakur has taken little solid food and has slept more than usual. There was no fever, no vomiting, no diarrhoea, no rash, and no overt bleeding. No recent travel. No known sick contacts.

Wen Thakur carries a documented diagnosis of iron-deficiency anaemia, for which she has been under follow-up. Vivek Thakur confirms that she has been on oral iron supplementation, though adherence has been inconsistent in recent weeks. Dr. Shreya Lindholm reviewed the available records and noted that the patient's iron-deficiency anaemia is the most likely explanation for the current presentation, pending investigation.

## Past Medical History

- Iron-deficiency anaemia — diagnosed previously, on oral iron
- No known drug allergies
- No prior surgeries
- Immunisations reported up to date by her mother

## Medications

Oral iron supplementation, dose and frequency to be confirmed with Vivek Thakur and Grace Okonkwo and reconciled by the admitting team. No other regular medications.

## Family History

Non-contributory. Vivek Thakur and Grace Okonkwo are both in good health. No family history of bleeding disorders or haematological malignancy.

## Social History

Wen Thakur lives at home with her father and her mother. She attends school. No safeguarding concerns identified at this time; both parents are engaged and cooperative.

## Examination on Admission

Wen Thakur appeared pale and mildly lethargic but was alert and responsive. Vital signs were recorded by the admitting nurse and are within acceptable limits for her age, with mild tachycardia noted. Conjunctivae pale. No jaundice. No lymphadenopathy. Heart sounds normal, no murmur. Chest clear on auscultation. Abdomen soft and non-tender. No organomegaly. No bruising or petechiae. Neurological examination grossly normal.

## Impression

Wen Thakur, a child with known iron-deficiency anaemia, presenting with worsening pallor, fatigue, and poor intake. Likely exacerbation of her underlying iron-deficiency anaemia. Differential includes other causes of anaemia, to be excluded with investigations.

## Plan

1. Admit to the paediatric ward under the care of Dr. Shreya Lindholm.
2. Baseline bloods including full blood count, iron studies, and reticulocyte count.
3. Continue iron therapy; consider parenteral iron if oral intolerance persists.
4. Monitor vital signs and oral intake.
5. Dietitian review.
6. Discuss admission deposit with the family — a hospital deposit of ₹92,000 has been recorded against Wen Thakur's account.
7. Keep Vivek Thakur and Grace Okonkwo updated; he and she have been given the ward contact details.

**BOARD NOTE — PROPOSED ACQUISITION OF Indus Bank BY Indus Realty**

**To:** Board of Directors, Indus Realty
**From:** Kavya Shah, Deal Lead
**Cc:** Kenji Nair, CFO
**Subject:** Project Sapphire — Recommendation to Proceed to Definitive Agreement
**Date:** For discussion at the next board meeting

**1. Purpose**
This note seeks the Board's approval to proceed with the proposed acquisition of Indus Bank by Indus Realty under the codename Project Sapphire. Kavya Shah has led diligence and negotiation; Kenji Nair has reviewed the financial case. Both recommend proceeding.

**2. Transaction summary**
Indus Realty proposes to acquire Indus Bank for a total consideration of $379 million. The target reported revenue of ₹1384 crore in its most recent fiscal year. The combined entity would create a diversified platform spanning real assets and financial services.

**3. Strategic rationale**
- Cross-sell of Indus Realty's property client base into Indus Bank's lending products.
- Diversification of group earnings away from cyclical real estate.
- Cost synergies in back-office and treasury functions.

**4. Diligence and advisers**
Michael Moreno, the group's external banker, has supported valuation work and confirms the $379 million range is defensible against comparable transactions. Kavya Shah notes that commercial diligence is substantially complete; legal and regulatory workstreams remain open. Kenji Nair has stress-tested the funding plan and is satisfied that the consideration is financeable without breaching existing covenants.

**5. Key risks**
- Regulatory approval timelines for a bank acquisition may extend beyond the current plan.
- Integration of Indus Bank's systems carries execution risk.
- Revenue of ₹1384 crore is concentrated in a small number of corporate relationships.

**6. Timeline and next steps**
The target deadline for signing the definitive agreement is June 19, 2026. To meet it, the Board is asked to approve the following:

**Patient:** Rehan Narayanan
**Medical Record Number:** MRN-2026-87856
**Date of Birth:** 17 January 1969
**Age:** 57 years old
**Weight:** 109 kg
**Attending Physician:** Anika Reddy, Rheumatology

## Admission and Discharge Diagnosis

Rehan Narayanan was admitted under the care of Anika Reddy for management of an acute flare of rheumatoid arthritis with significant polyarticular involvement and functional decline. Dr. Reddy is employed by Vardhan Hospital in the Department of Rheumatology.

## History of Presenting Illness

Mr. Narayanan, a 57 years old gentleman, presented with a two-week history of worsening joint pain and swelling affecting the hands, wrists, and knees. He reported morning stiffness lasting more than two hours and difficulty with activities of daily living. His known diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis had previously been managed on maintenance therapy. On examination, he weighed 109 kg, with synovitis noted in multiple small joints.

## Hospital Course

Dr. Reddy initiated intravenous corticosteroid therapy with gradual improvement in his symptoms. Baseline investigations were obtained, and the patient was reviewed by physiotherapy for mobility support. His weight of 109 kg was noted as a factor in joint loading, and dietary counselling was arranged. Mr. Narayanan remained hemodynamically stable throughout admission. He was transitioned to oral therapy and tolerated the change well.

Ananya Kapoor, his daughter, was involved in discussions regarding discharge planning and support at home. She confirmed that she would assist her father with medication adherence and follow-up appointments. Dr. Reddy met with Ms. Kapoor to review warning signs and when to seek urgent care.

## Discharge Medications

- Oral corticosteroids, tapering regimen as directed
- Disease-modifying antirheumatic therapy continued at adjusted dose
- Analgesia as required
- Calcium and vitamin D supplementation

## Discharge Condition

Rehan Narayanan was discharged in stable condition with improved joint symptoms and mobilising independently with a walking aid. His medical record number MRN-2026-87856 should be quoted in all correspondence.

## Follow-Up

The patient is to be reviewed by Anika Reddy in the rheumatology outpatient clinic in two weeks. Ananya Kapoor was advised to accompany him to this appointment. Repeat blood work is to be arranged prior to review.

## Discharge Instructions

Mr. Narayanan and his daughter were counselled on medication compliance, recognition of flare symptoms, and the importance of gradual activity progression. He was advised to continue physiotherapy exercises at home and to maintain a healthy weight to reduce joint stress.

---

Lakshmi Walsh delivered the drivetrain diagnostics update ahead of the agreed milestone. Ethan Novak has had a strong year. He took over the quarterly reporting pack when the team was short-staffed and he delivered it without missing a deadline. His analysis of the vendor spend data surfaced two duplicate contracts, and he flagged them to me before renewal. I would like him to receive a bonus at the upper end of the analyst band.

Vivek Nguyen's employee id is EMP-61741, and his salary is ₹231,287 per month. Given his position in the band, I recommend a solid bonus rather than an exceptional one, with the larger adjustment to be considered at the next salary review. Ananya Iyengar led the redesign of the customer onboarding flow, and the early results are very encouraging. Joint pain and swelling, worse over the past three weeks.

**From:** Imran Sood, Deal Lead, Northstar Pharma
**Cc:** Mei Iyengar, CFO, Northstar Pharma
**Subject:** Project Project Sapphire — Recommendation to Proceed to Confirmatory Phase

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's approval to advance Project Sapphire, the proposed acquisition of Meridian Retail by Northstar Pharma, to the confirmatory due diligence and definitive documentation phase.

**2. Strategic Rationale**

Meridian Retail operates a complementary retail and distribution footprint that would accelerate Northstar Pharma's direct-to-consumer channel. The target's most recent reported revenue was ₹2073 crore, and its store network offers immediate reach in markets where Northstar Pharma currently has limited presence. Imran Sood has led preliminary discussions and confirms that the target's management is receptive to a negotiated transaction.

**3. Financial Overview**

Mei Iyengar has reviewed the preliminary financial model. She notes that the target's revenue base of ₹2073 crore supports a valuation range consistent with the Board's stated return thresholds, subject to confirmatory diligence. The CFO recommends that any offer remain conditional on quality-of-earnings work and a clean working-capital adjustment. Her assessment will be circulated in full ahead of the next Board meeting.

**4. Advisers and Next Steps**

Lavanya Moreno, the appointed banker, has prepared indicative structuring options and will coordinate the diligence workstreams. She can be reached at lavanya.moreno92@yahoo.com for any questions from Directors. Imran Sood remains the primary point of contact for the transaction and can be reached on +91 82800 62745; he will provide weekly progress updates to the Board.

**5. Key Risks**

- Integration risk across retail operations unfamiliar to Northstar Pharma.
- Valuation sensitivity to the target's reported revenue of ₹2073 crore pending verification.
- Regulatory and competition clearance timelines.

**6. Recommendation**

The Board is asked to approve progression of Project Sapphire to confirmatory diligence, authorise Imran Sood and Mei Iyengar to engage advisers as required, and note that no binding offer will be made without further Board approval.

Re: Grievance Investigation — Outcome

This memo records the findings of the grievance Anil Iyengar raised concerning Mei Kim. Gaurav Reddy is employed by Meridian Ventures and conducted the investigation.

Allegation: Iyengar states that on 9 July 2024, Mei Kim made dismissive remarks about his rheumatoid arthritis and suggested he was using it to avoid work. He reports that she repeated the comments in front of a colleague.

Evidence reviewed: Reddy interviewed the complainant, the respondent (employee id DA/4820), and witness Isabel Santos. Santos confirms that Kim referred to his condition in a mocking tone during the exchange on 9 July 2024. Kim acknowledges the conversation but denies intending harm; she states she did not know the details of his rheumatoid arthritis.

Findings: On the balance of probabilities, Mei Kim's comments were inappropriate and breached Meridian Ventures' standards of conduct. The panel accepts Santos's account as credible.

Recommendations: A written warning for Kim; mandatory respect-in-the-workplace training for her; a review of reasonable adjustments for Iyengar; and a follow-up check with him in one month.

Kim and Iyengar were both reviewed; a reimbursement of Rs. 9,41,640 was approved for one of them.

Gaurav Reddy
Investigator, Meridian Ventures

**BOARD NOTE — PROJECT BLUEBIRD**

**To:** Board of Directors, Tarang Holdings
**From:** Anika Ramaswamy, Deal Lead, Tarang Holdings
**Co-presented by:** Rahul Gill, CFO, Tarang Holdings
**Subject:** Proposed acquisition of Redwood Foods — approval to proceed to confirmatory phase

**1. Purpose**

This note seeks the Board's approval to advance Project Bluebird, the proposed acquisition by Tarang Holdings of Redwood Foods, to the confirmatory due diligence and definitive documentation stage. Anika Ramaswamy will lead the transaction for Tarang Holdings; Rahul Gill will oversee financing and treasury workstreams. Amara Carter has been engaged as external banker to the transaction.

**2. Transaction summary**

Tarang Holdings proposes to acquire 100% of Redwood Foods at an enterprise value of ₹3367 crore. Redwood Foods reported revenue of $554 million in its most recent fiscal year, and the target's management team has indicated support for a negotiated transaction. The consideration is expected to be funded through a combination of committed debt facilities and balance-sheet cash; Rahul Gill will bring a detailed financing plan to the Board before signing.

**3. Strategic rationale**

The combination would extend Tarang Holdings' presence in packaged and branded foods, add complementary manufacturing capacity, and create cross-selling opportunities across existing distribution channels. Amara Carter's preliminary analysis indicates that synergies could be material, though she has cautioned that the estimates remain indicative pending diligence.

**4. Key risks and mitigants**

- **Valuation risk:** The ₹3367 crore price implies a premium to comparable transactions. Mitigant: confirmatory diligence focused on quality of earnings and working capital normalisation.
- **Financing risk:** Debt markets remain sensitive to rate movements. Mitigant: Rahul Gill is arranging committed facilities with staggered maturities.
- **Integration risk:** Retention of Redwood Foods' senior management is critical. Mitigant: retention packages to be negotiated pre-signing.
- **Regulatory risk:** Antitrust review is expected; Anika Ramaswamy will coordinate filings.

**5. Timeline**

The target signing deadline is November 13, 2027. To meet it, confirmatory diligence must commence within two weeks of Board approval. Anika Ramaswamy will circulate a detailed workplan; she can be reached on +91 97978 04920 for any Board queries ahead of the meeting.

**6. Recommendation**

The Board is asked to:

1. Approve advancement of Project Bluebird to confirmatory diligence;
2. Authorise Anika Ramaswamy and Rahul Gill to incur diligence and advisory costs within the approved budget; and
3. Note that a further Board approval will be sought before execution of definitive agreements.

Respectfully submitted,

Anika Ramaswamy
Deal Lead, Tarang Holdings

Rahul Gill
CFO, Tarang Holdings

# Quarterly Team Performance Summary — Q3

**Prepared by:** Meenakshi Joshi, Manager, Clinical Analytics
**Employer:** Acme Pharma
**Team covered:** Clinical Analytics & Reporting

## Overview

This summary reviews the performance of the three-person team reporting to Meenakshi Joshi at Acme Pharma during the quarter. She has managed Aditya Santos, Harpreet Santos, and Arjun Joshi throughout the period, and her assessment of each is set out below. All three are employed by Acme Pharma and contribute to the company's clinical data and reporting workstreams.

## Individual Performance

### Aditya Santos — Analyst

Aditya Santos had a strong quarter. He completed the reconciliation of trial datasets ahead of schedule, and his analysis notes were consistently clear enough for reviewers to act on without follow-up. Meenakshi Joshi notes that he has become the team's go-to person for query resolution. His salary is ₹10,28,000 per annum, and she considers him well placed for expanded responsibilities next quarter. Aditya should focus on documenting assumptions earlier in each analysis cycle.

### Harpreet Santos — Engineer

Harpreet Santos delivered the pipeline reliability improvements that her manager had flagged as the team's top technical priority. She reduced recurring failures in the reporting jobs and mentored colleagues on the new deployment process. Her salary stands at ₹36,39,000 per annum. Meenakshi Joshi regards her as the technical anchor of the group and recommends her for the platform modernisation workstream. The one development area for Harpreet is earlier escalation when dependencies slip.

### Arjun Joshi — Designer

Arjun Joshi redesigned the dashboard suite used by clinical stakeholders, and feedback from reviewers was overwhelmingly positive. He also introduced a component library that has cut design turnaround time. His annual bonus is ₹5,78,000 per annum, reflecting the impact of his work this quarter. She encourages him to involve engineering earlier in the design cycle so that his concepts move to build more smoothly.

## Team-Level Observations

- Delivery against quarterly commitments was strong across all three workstreams.
- Collaboration improved markedly; Aditya, Harpreet, and Arjun now review each other's work before it reaches Meenakshi Joshi.
- Documentation remains the weakest area collectively, and she has asked the team to adopt a shared template.
- Meenakshi Joshi will continue to manage all three directly, with fortnightly one-to-ones.

## Compensation Reference

For planning purposes, Meenakshi Joshi confirms the following details on record at Acme Pharma:

- Aditya Santos — salary: ₹10,28,000 per annum
- Harpreet Santos — salary: ₹36,39,000 per annum
- Arjun Joshi — annual bonus: ₹5,78,000 per annum
- Meenakshi Joshi — salary: ₹19,59,000 per annum

## Priorities for Next Quarter

1. Complete the platform modernisation scoping, led by Harpreet Santos.
2. Roll out the redesigned dashboards to the remaining stakeholder groups, led by Arjun Joshi.
3. Close the outstanding reconciliation backlog, led by Aditya Santos.
4. Establish a shared documentation standard across the team, owned by Meenakshi Joshi.

## Sign-off

Aditya and Meenakshi both met the committee this week. Aditya's reimbursement of ₹69 lakh has been approved.

Prepared and approved by Meenakshi Joshi, Manager, Acme Pharma. She thanks Aditya, Harpreet, and Arjun for her team's strong quarter and looks forward to building on it.

Tanya Chopra

**Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Inquiry — Final Findings**

**Matter:** Complaint filed by Olivia Walsh against Keerthi Moreno
**Employer:** Zenith Retail
**Incident date:** November 5, 2027
**Investigator:** Meenakshi Walsh, External POSH Investigator engaged by Zenith Retail

**1. Background**
Olivia Walsh (she/her), a member of the store operations team at Zenith Retail, submitted a written complaint alleging inappropriate and persistent conduct by her colleague Keerthi Moreno (she/her). Olivia Walsh disclosed that she lives with major depressive disorder, and stated that Keerthi Moreno's conduct aggravated her condition. Keerthi Moreno is recorded in company records under employee ID OZ/1903.

**2. Evidence and Witnesses**
The committee, led by Meenakshi Walsh, interviewed Olivia Walsh, Keerthi Moreno, and witness Anil Ansari (he/him). Anil Ansari stated that on November 5, 2027 he observed Keerthi Moreno making unwelcome remarks toward Olivia Walsh near the stockroom. He described her as visibly distressed afterward. Meenakshi Walsh reviewed rosters confirming both parties were on shift that day. Keerthi Moreno denied the remarks but acknowledged a personal disagreement with Olivia Walsh.

The committee finds, on the balance of probabilities, that Keerthi Moreno engaged in unwelcome verbal conduct of a sexual nature toward Olivia Walsh on November 5, 2027. Anil Ansari's account was consistent and credible. Keerthi Moreno's denial was not supported by any corroborating evidence.

- Issue a formal written warning to Keerthi Moreno (employee ID OZ/1903).
- Require her to complete mandatory POSH training.
- Adjust shift scheduling to minimise contact between Keerthi Moreno and Olivia Walsh.
- Offer Olivia Walsh counselling support, with attention to her major depressive disorder.
- Review Zenith Retail's reporting channels.

This inquiry was conducted independently and in confidence. Meenakshi Walsh confirms she is employed by Zenith Retail as an external investigator and has no personal interest in the outcome.
